description: Senart's pioneering edition of the Mahavastu, volume three — public-domain substitute for Jones's translation.

title: Geminus: Elementa Astronomiae (Manitius 1898)
creator: Geminus (K. Manitius, ed.)
description: Manitius's 1898 Teubner Greek text of Geminus's Introduction to Astronomy — public-domain substitute for Evans and Berggren's translation.

title: Athenaeus Mechanicus: On Machines (Wescher 1867)
creator: Athenaeus Mechanicus (C. Wescher, ed./trans.)
description: Wescher's 1867 Greek-French edition of the Greek writers on siege warfare, containing the complete text of Athenaeus Mechanicus's On Machines — public-domain substitute for Whitehead and Blyth.

title: Firmicus Maternus: Mathesis (1551)
creator: Julius Firmicus Maternus
description: The 1551 Latin edition of Firmicus's Mathesis, the great Roman astrological handbook — public-domain substitute for Bram's translation.

title: Dioscorides: De Materia Medica (Berendes 1902)
creator: Pedanius Dioscorides (Julius Berendes, trans.)
description: Berendes's 1902 German rendering of Dioscorides's De Materia Medica, the foundational ancient pharmacology — public-domain substitute for Osbaldeston's translation.

title: Aelian: On Animals and Historical Miscellany (Hercher 1858)
creator: Claudius Aelianus (R. Hercher, ed.)
description: Hercher's 1858 Didot edition of Aelian's complete surviving works — On Animals (17 books), Historical Miscellany, letters and fragments — public-domain substitute for the Scholfield and Wilson Loebs.

title: On the Track of Unknown Animals (Heuvelmans, 1958)
creator: Bernard Heuvelmans (Richard Garnett, trans.)
description: The founding text of cryptozoology: Heuvelmans' worldwide survey of unknown and out-of-place animals in seven parts and nineteen chapters — from the orang-pendek and the yeti to sea serpents and the mammoth of the taiga — in Richard Garnett's 1958 English translation, public domain.

title: Abominable Snowmen: Legend Come to Life (Sanderson, 1961)
creator: Ivan T. Sanderson
description: The first major English survey of yeti/sasquatch evidence: fourteen chapters of case reports from five continents plus appendices on footprint analysis and Himalayan fauna — Ivan T. Sanderson's 1961 classic, public domain.

title: F. von Bellingshausens Forschungsfahrten im Südlichen Eismeer, 1819–1821 (1902)
creator: Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen
description: The German edition (1902, public domain) of Bellingshausen's account of the 1819–1821 Russian Antarctic expedition — the voyage that first sighted the Antarctic continent — in six chapters from Kronstadt to the homecoming.

title: Ginza Rba — The Great Treasure of the Mandaeans (Mark Lidzbarski German translation, 1925)
creator: Anonymous Mandaean sages / Mark Lidzbarski (translator)
description: The complete Ginza Rba (Great Treasure), holy book of Mandaeism, in Lidzbarski's 1925 German translation — the standard scholarly version, public domain; includes the Mandaean creation story.

title: The Popol Vuh: The Mythic and Heroic Sagas of the Kiches (Lewis Spence, 1908)
creator: Anonymous K'iche' Maya / Lewis Spence (rendering)
description: The Maya book of creation and the Hero Twins in Lewis Spence's 1908 English rendering — the classic public-domain version; the single most important native text of the Americas.

title: The Ascension of Isaiah (R. H. Charles translation, 1900)
creator: Anonymous (early Christian pseudepigraphon) / R. H. Charles (translator)
description: The ancient martyrdom-and-vision text — Isaiah's ascent through the seven heavens — in R. H. Charles's 1900 standard English translation, public domain.

title: The Oxyrhynchus Sayings of Jesus — Greek Fragments of the Gospel of Thomas (Grenfell and Hunt, 1904)
creator: Anonymous (early Christian) / Grenfell and Hunt (editors)
description: The earliest-attested sayings of the Gospel of Thomas — the Greek Oxyrhynchus papyrus fragments with English translations (1904); the only public-domain edition of the Thomas material.

title: The Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha of the Old Testament, Vol. II: Pseudepigrapha (R. H. Charles, ed., 1913)
creator: R. H. Charles (editor)
description: R. H. Charles's landmark 1913 English edition of the Old Testament Pseudepigrapha — Jubilees, 1–2 Enoch, Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs, 2–3 Baruch, 4 Ezra, Psalms of Solomon, and more — the public-domain predecessor to Charlesworth's volume, staged as its substitute.

title: The Religion of the Samurai
creator: Kaiten Nukariya
description: Kaiten Nukariya's The Religion of the Samurai: A Study of Zen Philosophy and Discipline in China and Japan (1913) — the pioneering English exposition of Zen by a Japanese Soto scholar; substituted for the unlocatable 1899 Nukariya entry.

title: Ancient Times: A History of the Early World
creator: James Henry Breasted
description: James Henry Breasted's Ancient Times: A History of the Early World (1916) — the Oriental Institute founder's sweeping history of the ancient Near East, Egypt, Greece and Rome; substituted for the erroneous 'History of the Ancient World' entry.

title: La Russie et l'Église universelle
creator: Vladimir Solovyov (1853-1900)
description: Vladimir Solovyov's La Russie et l'Église universelle (1889) — the Russian philosopher's French masterwork on Russia's spiritual mission and church reunion, in the original French; PD substitute for the copyrighted 1948 Rees translation.

title: Masnavi I Ma'navi: The Spiritual Couplets
creator: Jalalu'ddin Rumi (1207-1273); E. H. Whinfield (translator)
description: E. H. Whinfield's 1898 complete abridged English verse translation of Rumi's Masnavi — the first complete English rendering; PD substitute for the copyrighted complete Nicholson edition.

title: The Gospel of Philip (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Valentinian sayings gospel; PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Apocalypse of Adam (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Adam’s revelation to Seth (NHC V,1); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Teachings of Silvanus (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Wisdom instruction (NHC VII,4); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: On the Origin of the World (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Sethian cosmology (NHC II,5); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Concept of Our Great Power (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Apocalyptic revelation (NHC VI,4); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: Trimorphic Protennoia (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Triple-formed Primal Thought (NHC XIII,1); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Acts of Peter and the Twelve Apostles (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Apostolic acts (NHC VI,1); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Gospel of Truth (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Valentinian meditation (NHC I,3); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Paraphrase of Shem (Mark M. Mattison translation, public domain)
creator: Mark M. Mattison
description: Sethian apocalypse (NHC VII,1); PD translation substitutes the restricted edition.

title: The Heart Sutra (F. Max Müller translation, SBE Vol. 49, 1894)
creator: F. Max Müller
description: Müller’s 1894 PD translation substitutes the restricted Red Pine 2004 commentary edition.

title: Ragnarok: The Age of Fire and Gravel
creator: Ignatius Donnelly
description: Donnelly's 1883 comet-catastrophism sequel to Atlantis — the founding text of modern catastrophist geology, cited from Velikovsky to Hancock.

title: The Great Cryptogram: Francis Bacon's Cipher in the So-Called Shakespeare Plays
creator: Ignatius Donnelly
description: Donnelly's 1888 Bacon-cipher magnum opus — the landmark of the Bacon-Shakespeare authorship controversy and the founding text of cryptogram literature.

title: The History of Atlantis
creator: Lewis Spence
description: Spence's 1927 synthesis — the most complete early scholarly survey of Atlantis theories, the standard interwar reference.

title: Atlantis in America
creator: Lewis Spence
description: Spence's 1925 New World volume — the key statement of the American-evidence case for Atlantis, pairing Plato with Mesoamerican archaeology.

title: Sacred Mysteries Among the Mayas and the Quiches, 11,500 Years Ago
creator: Augustus Le Plongeon
description: Le Plongeon's 1886 Maya-Atlantis manifesto — source of the name 'Mu' and the Maya-Egypt diffusion theory behind Donnelly and Churchward.

title: Paradise Found: The Cradle of the Human Race at the North Pole
creator: William F. Warren
description: Warren's 1885 Arctic-origin thesis — the founding text of the polar-Atlantis tradition, cited by theosophists ever since.

title: Ancient America, in Notes on American Archaeology
creator: John D. Baldwin
description: Baldwin's 1871 diffusionist classic — the most widely read 19th-century case for a lost civilized race in ancient America.

title: Lettres sur l'Atlantide de Platon et sur l'ancienne histoire de l'Asie
creator: Jean-Sylvain Bailly
description: Bailly's 1779 letters — the first modern scholarly treatise on Plato's Atlantis, in French; Donnelly's chief 18th-century predecessor.

title: Quatre lettres sur le Mexique
creator: Charles-Étienne Brasseur de Bourbourg
description: Brasseur's 1868 letters — the founding statement of the Maya-Atlantis connection by the great 19th-century Mayanist; in French.

title: Manuscrit Troano: Études sur le système graphique et la langue des Mayas, Vol. 1
creator: Charles-Étienne Brasseur de Bourbourg
description: First publication of the Troano Codex (1869), vol. 1 — the Maya manuscript Le Plongeon misread to coin 'Mu'; in French.

title: Manuscrit Troano: Études sur le système graphique et la langue des Mayas, Vol. 2
creator: Charles-Étienne Brasseur de Bourbourg
description: First publication of the Troano Codex, vol. 2 (1870), with Brasseur's conclusion and Maya phonetic table; in French.

title: Popol Vuh: Le livre sacré et les mythes de l'antiquité américaine
creator: Charles-Étienne Brasseur de Bourbourg, trans.
description: Brasseur's 1861 first European edition of the Popol Vuh — the Maya sacred book at the heart of every Maya-Atlantis theory; in French.

title: The Myths of the New World
creator: Daniel G. Brinton
description: Brinton's 1868 landmark — the great sceptical counterweight to diffusionism that every Atlantis writer had to answer.

title: American Antiquities, and Discoveries in the West
creator: Josiah Priest
description: Priest's 1833 bestseller — the first popular American 'lost race' book and the founding text of the mound-builder craze.

title: Ancient Monuments of the Mississippi Valley
creator: E. G. Squier and E. H. Davis
description: The 1848 Smithsonian survey — the foundational scientific record of the American mounds, cited in every lost-race debate since.

title: New Atlantis
creator: Francis Bacon
description: Bacon's 1627 island utopia of Bensalem — the archetype of the lost-continent tale in English, cited by Atlantis writers for three centuries.

title: Mythical Monsters
creator: Charles Gould
description: Gould's 1886 survey of dragons and sea-serpents — the founding text of cryptozoology and the 19th century's great fortean natural history.

title: 777 vel Prolegomena Symbolica ad Systemam Sceptico-Mysticae Viae Explicandae
creator: Aleister Crowley
description: Crowley's qabalistic correspondence tables for the 32 paths — the standard Thelemic reference work cited by every later writer on magical qabalah.

title: Konx Om Pax: Essays in Light
creator: Aleister Crowley
description: Crowley's early prose-poem essays on mysticism — the first book of his middle period, bridging his poetry and the later magical textbooks.

title: The Book of Lies, Which Is Also Falsely Called Breaks (Liber CCCXXXIII)
creator: Aleister Crowley
description: Crowley's book of 93 paradoxical chapters — the central Thelemic scripture of wit and contradiction, endlessly cited in Thelemic commentary.

title: Book 4, Part I: Mysticism
creator: Aleister Crowley (with Mary D'Este Sturges)
description: Part I of Crowley's great magical textbook — the systematic A.'.A.'. manual of mysticism, from asana to samadhi.

title: Book 4, Part II: Magick (Elementary Theory)
creator: Aleister Crowley (with Mary D'Este Sturges)
description: Part II of Crowley's great magical textbook — the elementary theory of magick: the temple, the circle, the triangle, and the weapons of the magician.

title: Moonchild (Liber LXXXI, The Butterfly Net)
creator: Aleister Crowley
description: Crowley's occult novel of a magical war over an unborn child — a roman-a-clef of the Golden Dawn and O.T.O. milieu, his major work of fiction.

title: The Diary of a Drug Fiend
creator: Aleister Crowley
description: Crowley's notorious novel of cocaine and heroin addiction — the book that made him infamous in the British press and a landmark of drug literature.

title: Psychic Self-Defense: A Study in Occult Pathology and Criminality
creator: Dion Fortune
description: Fortune's classic manual of defense against psychic attack — the foundational text of modern occult self-protection, cited in every later work on the subject.

title: The Esoteric Orders and Their Work
creator: Dion Fortune
description: Fortune's early survey of the Western esoteric orders and their methods — the first systematic English account of how the mystery schools actually work.

title: The Training and Work of an Initiate
creator: Dion Fortune
description: Fortune's companion to Esoteric Orders — the practical curriculum of occult initiation, from meditation to ceremonial work.

title: Sane Occultism
creator: Dion Fortune
description: Fortune's defense of rational occultism against credulity and fraud — the manifesto of her no-nonsense approach to esoteric study.

title: The Secrets of Dr. Taverner
creator: Dion Fortune
description: Fortune's classic occult detective stories — the founding text of esoteric fiction's 'psychic doctor' genre, blending her nursing and occult experience.

title: The Legend of Aleister Crowley
creator: P. R. Stephensen and Israel Regardie
description: The contemporary defense of Crowley against the press vilification campaign — the primary document of the 1930s battle over his reputation, by his future secretary.

title: The Tree of Life: A Study in Magic
creator: Israel Regardie
description: Regardie's great theoretical exposition of magic through the qabalistic Tree of Life — the systematic textbook behind his later Golden Dawn work.

title: The Star in the West: A Critical Essay upon the Works of Aleister Crowley
creator: J. F. C. Fuller
description: Fuller's pioneering critical study of Crowley — the first serious literary assessment of the poet-occultist, by the future military theorist.

title: Q.B.L., or The Bride's Reception
creator: Frater Achad (Charles Stansfeld Jones)
description: Achad's first major qabalistic work — the radical Thelemic reassignment of the Tree of Life attributions that split him from Crowley.

title: The Egyptian Revival, or The Ever-Coming Son in the Light of the Tarot
creator: Frater Achad (Charles Stansfeld Jones)
description: Achad's qabalistic revisionism applied to Egyptian symbolism and the tarot — the second of his three major Thelemic qabalistic texts.

title: The Anatomy of the Body of God
creator: Frater Achad (Charles Stansfeld Jones)
description: Achad's geometric projection of the Tree of Life in three dimensions — the culmination of his qabalistic trilogy, with Will Ransom's diagrams.

title: A Vision
creator: W. B. Yeats
description: Yeats's occult system of history and personality channeled through automatic writing — the central esoteric text of the 1920s literary occult revival.

title: Tertium Organum: The Third Canon of Thought
creator: P. D. Ouspensky
description: Ouspensky's exposition of the fourth dimension as the key to cosmic consciousness — the book that carried hyperspace philosophy into the occult revival.

title: A New Model of the Universe
creator: P. D. Ouspensky
description: Ouspensky's synthesis of science, religion, and esotericism — the full statement of his psychological method, never renewed for copyright.

title: The Pictorial Key to the Tarot
creator: A. E. Waite
description: Waite's definitive exposition of the Rider-Waite tarot — the book that fixed the meanings of the modern tarot deck for the next century.

title: The Holy Kabbalah
creator: A. E. Waite
description: Waite's massive historical study of the secret tradition in Israel — the standard English survey of Christian kabbalah in the early 20th century.

title: The Brotherhood of the Rosy Cross
creator: A. E. Waite
description: Waite's documentary history of Rosicrucianism — the scholarly foundation for all later study of the Rosy Cross legend.

title: The Serpent Power: The Secrets of Tantric and Shaktic Yoga
creator: Arthur Avalon (Sir John Woodroffe)
description: Woodroffe's translation and commentary on the Sat-cakra-nirupana — the book that introduced kundalini yoga to the West.

title: The Rosicrucian Cosmo-Conception, or Mystic Christianity
creator: Max Heindel
description: Heindel's Rosicrucian cosmology — the founding text of the American Rosicrucian movement, first published 1909; this is the 1929 printing.

title: The Witch-Cult in Western Europe
creator: Margaret Alice Murray
description: Murray's anthropological argument for a surviving pagan witch-religion — the most influential (and contested) witchcraft thesis of the 20th century.

title: An Experiment with Time
creator: J. W. Dunne
description: Dunne's theory of serial time and precognitive dreams — the book that made 'precognition' a subject of serious psychical research.

title: The Masters and the Path
creator: C. W. Leadbeater
description: Leadbeater's account of the Theosophical Masters and the occult hierarchy — the definitive statement of 1920s Theosophical esotericism.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 2 (September 1909)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 2 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (September 1909) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 3 (March 1910)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 3 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (March 1910) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 4 (September 1910)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 4 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (September 1910) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 5 (March 1911)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 5 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (March 1911) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 6 (September 1911)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 6 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (September 1911) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 7 (March 1912)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 7 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (March 1912) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 8 (September 1912)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 8 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (September 1912) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 9 (March 1913)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 9 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (March 1913) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 10 (September 1913)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: No. 10 of Crowley's magical journal The Equinox (September 1913) — the primary record of the A.'.A.'. and the birth of Thelema, containing first publications of the Holy Books and ritual corpus.

title: The Equinox, Vol. III, No. 1: The Blue Equinox (March 1919)
creator: Aleister Crowley (ed.)
description: The Blue Equinox — Crowley's O.T.O. manifesto number, containing the Gnostic Mass, the O.T.O. constitutions, and the proclamation of the Law of Thelema.

title: The Case for the Sea-Serpent
creator: Rupert T. Gould
description: Rupert Gould's 1930 naval officer's brief for the sea-serpent — the 20th century's most methodical pro-sea-serpent monograph, answering Oudemans case by case.

title: The Great Sea-Serpent: An Historical and Critical Treatise
creator: Antoon Cornelis Oudemans
description: Oudemans' 1892 treatise — the founding scientific monograph of sea-serpent research, analyzing 162 sighting reports; the book every later sea-serpent writer answers.

title: Sea Monsters Unmasked
creator: Henry Lee
description: Henry Lee's 1883 skeptical natural history of sea-serpents — the Victorian debunking classic explaining sightings via giant squid and known animals.

title: Sea Fables Explained
creator: Henry Lee
description: Lee's 1883 companion volume dissecting mermaids, the kraken, and sea-fables — the great Victorian demystification of mermaid lore.

title: The Octopus; or, The Devil-Fish of Fiction and of Fact
creator: Henry Lee
description: Lee's 1875 monograph on the octopus and the kraken legend — the first scientific treatment separating the real devil-fish from the mythic kraken.

title: Monsters of the Sea, Legendary and Authentic
creator: John Gibson
description: Gibson's 1887 survey of sea monsters legendary and authentic — from the kraken and sea-serpent to the giant squid, a Victorian bestiary of the deep.

title: The Wilderness Hunter
creator: Theodore Roosevelt
description: Roosevelt's 1893 hunting memoir containing the famous 'Bauman' story — the trapper stalked by a mysterious bipedal beast, the classic proto-Bigfoot account.

title: Beasts and Men
creator: Carl Hagenbeck
description: Hagenbeck's 1910 memoir — the famous animal dealer who first published Western reports of a giant Congo dinosaur, the origin of the Mokele-mbembe story.

title: Mount Everest: The Reconnaissance, 1921
creator: Charles Howard-Bury and the Mount Everest Committee
description: The official 1922 account of the 1921 Everest reconnaissance — containing the first published report of the 'Metohkangmi' tracks that became the Abominable Snowman.

title: Through Tibet to Everest
creator: John B. L. Noel
description: Captain Noel's 1927 Everest book with a chapter on the 'Legendary Hairy Man of the Mountains' — an early mountaineer's treatment of yeti lore.

title: Three Voyages of a Naturalist
creator: Michael J. Nicoll
description: Nicoll's 1908 natural-history voyages, including his 1905 'Valhalla' sea-serpent sighting off Brazil — one of the most credible 20th-century reports, debated by Gould.

title: Explorations and Adventures in Equatorial Africa
creator: Paul Du Chaillu
description: Du Chaillu's 1861 bestseller — the book that introduced the gorilla to the popular imagination, the 'monster ape' narrative that made the gorilla famous.

title: Trailing the Giant Panda
creator: Theodore Roosevelt Jr. and Kermit Roosevelt
description: The Roosevelt brothers' 1929 account of the expedition that brought the first giant panda to the West — the 'mystery bear' of Tibet made real.

title: In Brightest Africa
creator: Carl E. Akeley
description: Akeley's 1923 classic of African natural history and gorilla study — the taxidermist-conservationist who made the mountain gorilla known to museums.

title: On the Gorilla Trail
creator: Mary Hastings Bradley
description: Bradley's 1922 account — among the first books on the mountain gorilla, by one of the first women to seek it in the Virungas.

title: Two Trips to Gorilla Land and the Cataracts of the Congo
creator: Richard Francis Burton
description: Burton's 1876 narrative of seeking the gorilla in Gaboon — the great explorer's contribution to the 19th-century gorilla literature.

title: The Wonderland of the Eastern Congo
creator: T. Alexander Barns
description: Barns' 1922 account of the snow-crowned volcanoes region — early 20th-century gorilla country at the dawn of mountain-gorilla science.

title: Among the Himalayas
creator: Laurence Austine Waddell
description: Waddell's 1899 Himalayan travelogue recording legends of 'hairy wild men' — one of the earliest Western notices of yeti folklore.

title: The Kangchenjunga Adventure
creator: Frank S. Smythe
description: Smythe's 1930 account of the 1929 Kangchenjunga expedition, reporting 'footprints of a Snow Man' — a mountaineer's yeti encounter.

title: Account of a Photographic Expedition to the Southern Glaciers of Kangchenjunga in the Sikkim Himalaya
creator: N. A. Tombazi
description: Tombazi's 1926 expedition book containing the famous first-hand 1925 yeti sighting — the 'reported wild man' seen at 15,500 feet, with measured footprints.

title: The Romance of Natural History
creator: Philip Henry Gosse
description: Gosse's 1860 popular natural history treating sea-serpents and ocean marvels as 'romance' — the Victorian naturalist's take on sea monsters, cited by Oudemans.

title: The Lost World
creator: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Doyle's 1912 novel of living dinosaurs on a South American plateau — the fiction that created the 'lost world' trope driving real cryptozoological expeditions.

title: The Cruise of the 'Cachalot'
creator: Frank T. Bullen
description: Bullen's 1898 whaling classic with the famous giant-squid account — a whaleman's first-hand sea-monster narrative from the age of sail.

title: Denizens of the Deep
creator: Frank T. Bullen
description: Bullen's 1904 volume on deep-sea life, treating sea-serpents and ocean monsters from a sailor-naturalist's experience.

title: "What Is It? A Strange Creature Captured above Yale — A British Columbia Gorilla"
creator: Daily British Colonist (Victoria, B.C.)
description: The July 4, 1884 British Colonist report of 'Jacko,' the ape-like creature captured near Yale — the famous proto-Bigfoot capture story, likely a hoax, endlessly cited.

title: "Introducing B.C.'s Hairy Giants"
creator: J. W. Burns
description: Burns' April 1929 Maclean's article — the first publication to use the word 'Sasquatch' in English, launching the modern Bigfoot era.

title: Report of a Committee of the Linnaean Society of New England, Relative to a Large Marine Animal, Supposed to Be a Serpent, Seen near Cape Ann, Massachusetts, in August 1817
creator: Linnaean Society of New England
description: The 1817 Linnaean Society report on the Gloucester sea-serpent — the first organized scientific investigation of a sea-serpent, with sworn depositions.

title: The Stronsa Beast: Dr. Barclay's Account with Affidavits (1808–1809)
creator: Dr. John Barclay; Wernerian Natural History Society
description: Barclay's 1808–09 Wernerian Society papers on the Stronsa carcass with sworn affidavits — the 'sea-serpent' specimen later identified as a basking shark.

title: The Daedalus Sea-Serpent Reports (1848)
creator: Capt. Peter M'Quhae; Lieut. Edgar Drummond; The Zoologist
description: The complete 1848 Daedalus dossier from The Zoologist — M'Quhae's Admiralty report, Drummond's journal, Times reprints, and the Daphne account; the classic sea-serpent sighting.

title: "Notice of the External Characters and Habits of Troglodytes gorilla"
creator: Thomas S. Savage
description: Savage's 1847 paper naming the gorilla to science — the founding document that turned the 'wild man of the woods' from legend into zoology.

title: "The Quest for the Dragon of Komodo"
creator: W. Douglas Burden
description: Burden's 1927 Natural History account of the expedition that captured the Komodo dragon — the 'living dragon' brought to America, an inspiration for King Kong.

title: Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects (The Condon Report)
creator: University of Colorado / Dr. Edward U. Condon (USAF contract)
description: The complete 1968 USAF-commissioned scientific study of UFOs that ended Project Blue Book; its 'no further study warranted' conclusion is the pivotal document in government ufology, staged here with the full index.
source: National Center for Atmospheric Research mirror (ncas.org)

title: Unidentified Flying Objects: Hearings Before the Committee on Armed Services, U.S. House of Representatives (April 5, 1966)
creator: U.S. House Committee on Armed Services
description: Complete April 1966 House Armed Services hearing on UFOs, including J. Allen Hynek's testimony; the hearing that forced the Air Force toward the Condon study.

title: Project MKULTRA, the CIA’s Program of Research in Behavioral Modification: Joint Hearing Before the Select Committee on Intelligence and the Subcommittee on Health and Scientific Research (August 3, 1977)
creator: U.S. Senate Select Committee on Intelligence / Committee on Human Resources
description: Complete August 1977 joint Senate hearing on CIA Project MKULTRA, convened after the 1977 financial-records recovery; the foundational public record on the mind-control program.

title: KUBARK Counterintelligence Interrogation (CIA interrogation manual)
creator: Central Intelligence Agency
description: The CIA's declassified 1963 counterintelligence interrogation manual, the template for later interrogation doctrine; pivotal for understanding Cold War intelligence practice.

title: CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947–90
creator: Gerald K. Haines (CIA History Staff), Studies in Intelligence
description: Official CIA in-house history of the Agency's UFO involvement 1947-1990, from the Arnold wave and Robertson Panel through the 1970s; the Agency's own account of its role.

title: STAR GATE Program Summary (Defense Intelligence Agency, 15 May 1991)
creator: Defense Intelligence Agency
description: Declassified 1991 DIA summary of the STAR GATE remote-viewing intelligence program; the program's own official overview.

title: Mars Exploration, May 22, 1984 (STAR GATE remote-viewing session transcript)
creator: U.S. Army / STAR GATE program
description: Declassified transcript of the 22 May 1984 STAR GATE remote-viewing session targeting Mars one million years B.C.; the most famous single session of the program.

title: Analysis and Assessment of Gateway Process (U.S. Army INSCOM, 9 June 1983)
creator: Lt. Col. Wayne M. McDonnell / U.S. Army Intelligence and Security Command
description: Declassified 1983 Army INSCOM analysis of the Monroe Institute's Gateway consciousness-altering process; the military's serious assessment of altered-states techniques.

title: Coordinate Remote Viewing Manual (1 May 1986)
creator: Defense Intelligence Agency / STAR GATE ( SRI International lineage; manual compiled for DIA)
description: The declassified DIA coordinate remote viewing training manual (originally dated 1 May 1986, Ingo Swann method); the program's core instructional document.

creator: Edward William Nelson
description: The Bureau of American Ethnology's great Bering Strait monograph — the definitive 19th-century record of Yupik shamanism and ceremony.

title: Ethnological Results of the Point Barrow Expedition
creator: John Murdoch
description: The Point Barrow expedition's ethnology — Iñupiat shamanic practice and material culture documented at the edge of first contact.

title: Beschreibung von dem Lande Kamtschatka
creator: Georg Wilhelm Steller
description: Steller's 1774 Kamchatka description — the earliest European eyewitness account of Itelmen shamanism, from Bering's expedition naturalist. In German.

title: Shamanism in Siberia and European Russia
creator: V. M. Mikhailowski
description: The first English-language survey paper to define 'shamanism' for Western anthropology (Journal of the Anthropological Institute, 1895), translated by Oliver Wardrop.

title: Barddas
creator: Iolo Morganwg (ed. J. Williams ab Ithel)
description: Iolo Morganwg's 'Bardic-Druidic' theology, presented as ancient but largely his own invention — the forgery that shaped the entire modern druid revival. (Text of the 1862/1874 edition.)

title: The Mythology and Rites of the British Druids
creator: Edward Davies
description: Davies's 1809 druidic mythology — the Romantic era's grand system fusing Noah's Flood, the ark, and druid lore; the book that defined 'druidism' for a generation.

title: Celtic Researches
creator: Edward Davies
description: Davies's 1804 origin-treatise on the ancient Britons — the first Romantic attempt at a systematic Celtic-druidic prehistory.

title: A Critical History of the Celtic Religion and Learning
creator: John Toland
description: Toland's posthumous 1726 history (this text from the 1815 edition) — the Enlightenment's first critical, demystifying account of the druids.

title: The Druids: A Study in Keltic Prehistory
creator: T. D. Kendrick
description: Kendrick's 1927 synthesis (this text from the 1928 impression) — the first modern scholarly druid study, the baseline for all later work.

title: The Myvyrian Archaiology of Wales
creator: Owen Jones, Edward Williams, and William Owen Pughe (eds.)
description: The great Welsh manuscript collection (1801–1807; this text from the 1870 reprint) — the print vehicle through which Iolo Morganwg's druidic forgeries entered the tradition.

title: Mona Antiqua Restaurata
creator: Henry Rowlands
description: Rowlands's Anglesey antiquities (this text from the 1766 second edition) — the first druid-centered archaeology of Mona, founding the 'druidical temple' reading of megaliths.

title: Lectures on the Origin and Growth of Religion as Illustrated by Celtic Heathendom
creator: John Rhŷs
description: Rhŷs's 1888 Hibbert Lectures — the founding academic work on Celtic pagan religion, still cited on druidic belief.

title: Celtic Folklore: Welsh and Manx
creator: John Rhŷs
description: Rhŷs's two-volume folklore collection (1901) — druidic survivals traced through Welsh and Manx folk belief, fairies, and folk-heroes.

title: Les druides et les dieux celtiques à forme d'animaux
creator: Henri d'Arbois de Jubainville
description: D'Arbois de Jubainville's 1906 study — the French Celtic school's authority on druidic religion and animal-formed gods. In French.

title: The Mysteries of Britain
creator: Lewis Spence
description: Spence's 1928 survey of Britain's secret rites and traditions — druids, megaliths, and the native mystery tradition restored.

title: Runir seu Danica literatura antiquissima
creator: Ole Worm
description: Worm's runology (this text from the 1651 second edition) — the first scholarly treatment of the runes; the founding work of runic studies. In Latin.

title: Handbook of the Old-Northern Runic Monuments
creator: George Stephens
description: Stephens's 1884 handbook — the 19th century's standard English guide to the runic monuments of Scandinavia and England, by the great runologist.

title: Teutonic Mythology
creator: Jacob Grimm (trans. James Steven Stallybrass)
description: Grimm's Deutsche Mythologie in Stallybrass's English (4 vols., 1880–1888) — the foundation text of Germanic myth and rune-lore; every later work cites it.

title: Die Runenschrift
creator: Ludvig Wimmer
description: Wimmer's 1887 runology — the Danish school's definitive 19th-century study of the runic alphabet. In German.

title: Greeks and Goths: A Study on the Runes
creator: Isaac Taylor
description: Taylor's 1879 rune-origin theory — the Victorian debate on the runes' debt to the Greek alphabet, a turning point in runology.

title: Atalanta fugiens
creator: Michael Maier
description: Maier's 1618 alchemical emblem book — 50 emblems with epigrams, discourses, and musical fugues; the Rosicrucian era's most famous alchemical art-text. In Latin.

title: Amulets and Superstitions
creator: E. A. Wallis Budge
description: Budge's 1930 compendium (reprinted as 'Amulets and Talismans') — the classic English survey of Egyptian and Near Eastern amulets, with original texts and translations.

title: Amulets
creator: W. M. Flinders Petrie
description: Petrie's 1914 illustrated corpus — the great excavator's typology of Egyptian amulets, the archaeological foundation of the subject.

title: Les vrayes centuries et propheties
creator: Michel de Nostredame
description: Nostradamus's Centuries in the original French (1710 edition) — the prophecies as his readers first met them. In French.

title: The True Prophecies or Prognostications of Michael Nostradamus
creator: Michel de Nostredame (trans. Theophilus de Garencières)
description: Garencières's 1672 English translation — the first complete English Nostradamus, with the famous biographical preface; the version that made him an English prophet.

title: The Geomancie of Maister Christopher Cattan
creator: Christopher Cattan (trans. Francis Sparry)
description: Cattan's 1591 geomancy in Sparry's English — the first English manual of divination by earth-figures, the foundation of English geomantic literature.

title: Palmistry, the Secrets Thereof Disclosed
creator: Richard Saunders
description: Saunders's 1663 palmistry — the Restoration era's standard English chiromancy manual, reprinted for a century.

title: The Romance and Prophecies of Thomas of Erceldoune
creator: Thomas of Erceldoune (ed. James A. H. Murray)
description: Murray's 1875 Early English Text Society edition — Thomas the Rhymer's romance and the Scottish political-prophecy tradition in full.

title: The Strange and Wonderful Prophecies of Mother Shipton
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1700 Mother Shipton collection — England's great folk-prophetess in her classic chapbook form: birth, life, death, and prophecies.

title: The Essays and Hymns of Synesius of Cyrene
creator: Synesius of Cyrene (trans. Augustine Fitzgerald)
description: Fitzgerald's 1930 translation (2 vols.) — includes De insomniis, the Neoplatonic theory of divination by dreams, the late-antique classic on the subject.

title: A Dweller on Two Planets
creator: Frederick S. Oliver (as 'Phylos the Thibetan')
description: Oliver's 1905 theosophical novel, dictated by the discarnate 'Phylos' — Atlantis, Lemuria, and occult science; the pivotal American occult novel.

title: Perpetuum Mobile; or, Search for Self-Motive Power
creator: Henry Dircks
description: The great Victorian survey of three centuries of perpetual-motion schemes — the essential history of the obsession, cataloguing every known device and delusion.

title: Perpetuum Mobile; or, Search for Self-Motive Power, Second Series
creator: Henry Dircks
description: Dircks's second series, continuing his exhaustive catalogue of perpetual-motion machines and their inventors — the companion volume to the 1861 survey.

title: A Lecture on the Perpetual Motion
creator: William Kenrick
description: An 18th-century public lecture demolishing perpetual-motion claims — a contemporary debunking from the height of the craze.

title: Remarks on Some Attempts Made towards a Perpetual Motion
creator: John Theophilus Desaguliers
description: The Royal Society's great experimentalist takes apart perpetual-motion wheels in the Philosophical Transactions — the early-18th-century scientific verdict.

title: Perpetual Motion
creator: George Chrystal
description: The Encyclopaedia Britannica's authoritative survey of perpetual motion — the establishment's final word, from thermodynamics to the 1775 Academy ban.

title: Zymotechnia Fundamentalis
creator: Georg Ernst Stahl
description: Stahl's foundational Latin text of the phlogiston theory — the doctrine of the 'inflammable principle' that ruled chemistry for most of the 18th century.

title: Experiments upon Magnesia Alba, Quick-Lime, and Other Alcaline Substances
creator: Joseph Black
description: Black's discovery of 'fixed air' (carbon dioxide) — the quantitative experiments that cracked phlogiston's foundations before Lavoisier.

title: Experiments and Observations on Different Kinds of Air
creator: Joseph Priestley
description: Priestley's complete three-volume series (1774-77) — the isolation of oxygen ('dephlogisticated air') by phlogiston's greatest defender, the experiments Lavoisier reinterpreted to kill the theory.

title: Chemical Observations and Experiments on Air and Fire
creator: Carl Wilhelm Scheele
description: Scheele's independent discovery of oxygen ('fire air') — the Swedish apothecary who found it before Priestley published, in English translation.

title: An Essay on Phlogiston, and the Constitution of Acids
creator: Richard Kirwan
description: The last great systematic defense of phlogiston — the book that forced Lavoisier's circle to answer every objection in print.

title: Essai sur le phlogistique, et sur la constitution des acides
creator: Antoine de Fourcroy et al.
description: The French chemists' annotated translation of Kirwan — Morveau, Lavoisier, Laplace, Monge, Berthollet and Fourcroy refuting phlogiston point by point in the notes; the theory's death certificate, in French.

title: Elements of Chemistry, In a New Systematic Order
creator: Antoine Lavoisier
description: Lavoisier's Traité élémentaire de chimie in Robert Kerr's 1790 English translation — the book that buried phlogiston and founded modern chemistry.

title: Method of Chymical Nomenclature
creator: Louis-Bernard Guyton de Morveau
description: The new chemical nomenclature of 1787 in English — the linguistic arm of the Chemical Revolution, renaming the substances phlogiston theory had misnamed.

title: Experiments on Air
creator: Henry Cavendish
description: Cavendish's 1784-85 papers establishing the compound nature of water — the experimental fact that made phlogiston untenable, plus his answer to Kirwan.

title: Experiments on the Generation of Insects
creator: Francesco Redi
description: Redi's 1668 experiments with meat and maggots — the first controlled blow against spontaneous generation, in the 1909 Bigelow translation.

title: A Summary of Some Late Observations upon the Generation, Composition, and Decomposition of Animal and Vegetable Substances
creator: John Turberville Needham
description: Needham's Royal Society paper claiming microscopic proof of spontaneous generation — the claim Spallanzani and Pasteur spent a century demolishing.

title: Dissertations Relative to the Natural History of Animals and Vegetables
creator: Lazzaro Spallanzani
description: Spallanzani's great English work on generation — the two-volume experimental answer to Needham and Buffon that first made spontaneous generation scientifically untenable.

title: Hétérogénie; ou, Traité de la génération spontanée
creator: Félix-Archimède Pouchet
description: Pouchet's massive 1859 treatise reviving spontaneous generation — the book that goaded the French Academy into the Pouchet-Pasteur prize contest of the 1860s. In French.

title: Sur les corpuscules organisés qui existent dans l'atmosphère: examen de la doctrine des générations spontanées
creator: Louis Pasteur
description: Pasteur's 1861 memoir and Sorbonne-period lecture demolishing spontaneous generation — the swan-neck flask experiments that ended the debate. In French.

title: Essays on the Floating-Matter of the Air in Relation to Putrefaction and Infection
creator: John Tyndall
description: Tyndall's optically-pure-air experiments confirming Pasteur in England and crushing Bastian's heterogenesis — the final experimental word on spontaneous generation.

title: The Beginnings of Life
creator: Henry Charlton Bastian
description: Bastian's two-volume revival of spontaneous generation (heterogenesis) — the last serious scientific defense, answered by Tyndall and Pasteur.

title: The Bakerian Lecture: On the Theory of Light and Colours
creator: Thomas Young
description: Young's 1801-02 Bakerian lecture reviving the wave theory of light — the paper that made the luminiferous ether scientifically necessary.

title: A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field
creator: James Clerk Maxwell
description: Maxwell's 1865 memoir unifying electricity, magnetism and light in the electromagnetic ether — the theory Michelson set out to test.

title: Ether
creator: James Clerk Maxwell
description: Maxwell's Encyclopaedia Britannica article on the ether — the great theorist's own summary of what the luminiferous medium was supposed to be.

title: The Relative Motion of the Earth and the Luminiferous Ether
creator: Albert A. Michelson
description: Michelson's 1881 Potsdam experiment — the first attempt to detect Earth's motion through the ether, whose null result started the crisis.

title: On the Relative Motion of the Earth and the Luminiferous Ether
creator: Albert A. Michelson and Edward W. Morley
description: The Michelson-Morley null result of 1887 — the most famous failed experiment in physics, and the empirical fact relativity was built to explain.

title: The Ether of Space
creator: Oliver Lodge
description: Lodge's popular exposition of the ether at its zenith — the last great defense of the medium just as relativity was rendering it superfluous.

title: Modern Views of Electricity
creator: Oliver Lodge
description: Lodge's 1892 treatise on electricity as ether mechanics — the high-water mark of Victorian ether physics, with lightning and discharge experiments.

title: Aether and Matter
creator: Joseph Larmor
description: Larmor's 1900 development of an electron theory of the ether — the most sophisticated ether model ever built, published five years before Einstein.

title: The Foundations of Science: Science and Hypothesis, The Value of Science, Science and Method
creator: Henri Poincaré
description: Poincaré's three great books on science — including the conventionalist philosophy and the relativity principle he stated before Einstein, in Halsted's translation.

title: On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies
creator: Albert Einstein
description: Einstein's 1905 special relativity paper — the paper that killed the ether, deriving its effects from two postulates with no medium at all. Saha's 1920 translation.

title: The Theory of Electrons and Its Applications to the Phenomena of Light and Radiant Heat
creator: Hendrik Antoon Lorentz
description: Lorentz's Columbia lectures on the electron theory — the ether's last rigorous formulation, including the contraction hypothesis, by the theory's co-creator.

title: "N" Rays: A Collection of Papers Communicated to the Academy of Sciences
creator: René Blondlot
description: Blondlot's collected N-ray papers — the complete primary record of France's great pathological-science episode, in Julien Garcin's English translation.

title: The n-Rays
creator: Robert W. Wood
description: Wood's devastating 1904 Nature letter from Blondlot's own laboratory — the three-hour visit that exposed N-rays as self-deception; the founding document of pathological science.

title: Circular No. 1
creator: John Cleves Symmes
description: Symmes's 1818 circular declaring the earth hollow and open at the poles — the founding document of the American hollow-earth movement.

title: Symzonia: Voyage of Discovery
creator: Captain Adam Seaborn
description: The first hollow-earth novel — a voyage through Symmes's polar opening to the inner world of Symzonia, the book that launched the subterranean-fiction tradition.

title: Symmes's Theory of Concentric Spheres
creator: James McBride
description: McBride's 1826 exposition of Symmes's hollow-earth system — the movement's first full-dress scientific apologia, ending with FINIS.

title: Remarks on a Review of Symmes' Theory, which Appeared in the American Quarterly Review
creator: Jeremiah N. Reynolds
description: Reynolds's 1827 rebuttal defending Symmes against the critics — the polemic that carried hollow-earth advocacy from pamphlets toward Congress.

title: Etidorhpa; or, The End of Earth
creator: John Uri Lloyd
description: The great American hollow-earth novel — a guided journey to the earth's core blending alchemy, geology and mysticism, the genre's classic.

title: The Cellular Cosmogony; or, The Earth a Concave Sphere
creator: Cyrus R. Teed (Koresh)
description: Koresh's cellular cosmogony — the inside-out hollow earth (we live within the sphere) with Morrow's 'New Geodesy' survey proofs; American fringe cosmology's bible.

title: A Journey to the Earth's Interior; or, Have the Poles Really Been Discovered?
creator: Marshall B. Gardner
description: Gardner's 1920 revised hollow-earth treatise — mammoths at the poles, the polar openings, and the case that Peary and Cook found nothing; the 20th century's fullest statement.

title: Mars
creator: Percival Lowell
description: Lowell's 1895 Mars — the book that launched the canal craze, arguing the Martian markings were the irrigation works of a dying civilization.

title: Mars and Its Canals
creator: Percival Lowell
description: Lowell's mature 1906 statement of the canal theory — eleven more years of Flagstaff observations marshalled for intelligent life on Mars.

title: Mars as the Abode of Life
creator: Percival Lowell
description: Lowell's 1908 popular synthesis — the full habitability argument, from polar caps to the physics of a dying planet's last inhabitants.

title: Is Mars Habitable?
creator: Alfred Russel Wallace
description: Wallace's 1907 demolition of Lowell's canals — the co-discoverer of natural selection shows Mars is airless, freezing and lifeless; the theory's death warrant.

title: Primitive Industry
creator: Charles Conrad Abbott
description: Abbott's 1881 Trenton-gravels monograph — America's first claim to a palaeolithic, the edifice Hrdlička would later dismantle stone by stone.

title: The Anthropological Treatises of Johann Friedrich Blumenbach
creator: Johann Friedrich Blumenbach (translated by Thomas Bendyshe)
description: Bendyshe's 1865 English edition of Blumenbach's treatises — the five-race classification that framed all 19th-century physical anthropology.

title: Antiquités celtiques et antédiluviennes, Tome I
creator: Jacques Boucher de Perthes
description: The 1847 volume claiming worked flints alongside extinct animals — the founding text of human antiquity, vindicated by Prestwich in 1859.

title: L'homme fossile de La Chapelle-aux-Saints
creator: Marcellin Boule
description: Boule's 1911 La Chapelle-aux-Saints memoir — the stooped, brutish Neanderthal reconstruction that defined the species' image for forty years.

title: On the Crania and Bones of Les Eyzies; or, The Ancient Cave-Men of the Périgord
creator: Paul Broca
description: Broca's 1868 Eyzies memoir in English — the first scientific description of the Cro-Magnon skeletons.

title: Reliquiae Diluvianae
creator: William Buckland
description: Buckland's 1823 cave-palaeontology classic — the diluvial framework every human-antiquity pioneer had to argue against.

title: Pithecoid Priscan Man from Gibraltar
creator: George Busk
description: Busk's July 1864 letter — the first published account of the Gibraltar Neanderthal skull, the fossil that confirmed Neanderthal was no one-off.

title: Essay on the Theory of the Earth
creator: Georges Cuvier (translated by Robert Kerr)
description: Cuvier's catastrophist geology in English — the authority whose 'no fossil man' dictum the antiquity pioneers spent fifty years overturning.

title: The Races of Man
creator: Joseph Deniker
description: Deniker's 1900 English 'Races of Man' — the 29-race classification that replaced Blumenbach's five and framed 20th-century physical anthropology.

title: De proto-Australische fossiele Mensch van Wadjak, Java (Tweede mededeeling)
creator: Eugène Dubois
description: Dubois's 1920 Wadjak memoir — the 'proto-Australian' Java skulls he kept back for thirty years, linking Java to Australia.

title: Morphology and Anthropology
creator: W. L. H. Duckworth
description: Duckworth's 1904 Cambridge synthesis of primate morphology and human evolution — the anatomical bridge to fossil man.

title: The Fossil Man of Abbeville. Again.
creator: Anonymous (Anthropological Review)
description: The 1864 follow-up on Boucher de Perthes's Abbeville finds — the Moulin-Quignon controversy record as new bones kept appearing.

title: La race humaine de Neanderthal ou de Canstadt en Belgique
creator: Julien Fraipont and Max Lohest
description: Fraipont and Lohest's 1886 Spy memoir — two Neanderthal skeletons with Mousterian tools that made the Neanderthal race undeniable.

title: An Account of Flint Weapons Discovered at Hoxne in Suffolk
creator: John Frere
description: Frere's 1800 letter — the first printed claim of deep human antiquity, weapons 'fabricated and used by a people who had not the use of metals,' ignored for sixty years.

title: Der fossile Mensch aus dem Neanderthal und sein Verhältniss zum Alter des Menschengeschlechts
creator: Johann Carl Fuhlrott
description: Fuhlrott's 1865 book — the Neanderthal discoverer's full case for the fossil's antiquity, expanding his 1859 first paper.

title: Prehistoric Europe: A Geological Sketch
creator: James Geikie
description: Geikie's 1881 glacial geology of human antiquity — the ice-age framework that gave palaeolithic man his chronology.

title: Notes on the Type of Hesperopithecus haroldcookii
creator: William K. Gregory and Milo Hellman
description: Gregory and Hellman's 1923 re-study of the Hesperopithecus tooth — the careful anatomy that began the walk-back from 'Nebraska Man'.

title: Further Notes on the Molars of Hesperopithecus and of Pithecanthropus
creator: William K. Gregory and Milo Hellman (appendix by Gerrit S. Miller Jr.)
description: Gregory, Hellman and Miller's 1923 molar comparison — Hesperopithecus measured against Pithecanthropus tooth by tooth.

title: Preliminary Revision of the Evidence Relating to Auriferous Gravel Man in California
creator: William Henry Holmes
description: Holmes's 1899 demolition of the Calaveras skull and the California 'auriferous gravel man' — the paper that closed the American deep-antiquity case.

title: Ancient Types of Man
creator: Arthur Keith
description: Keith's 1911 popular survey of fossil man — the book that taught a generation the Piltdown-to-Neanderthal story, with his famous Gibraltar reconstruction.

title: The Discovery of Fossil Remains of Man in Java, Australia, and South Africa
creator: Arthur Keith
description: Keith's 1921 Nature roundup — Wadjak, Talgai and Boskop man in one sweeping survey of the new fossil geography.

title: Reliquiae Aquitanicae
creator: Édouard Lartet and Henry Christy (edited by Thomas Rupert Jones)
description: Lartet and Christy's 1865–75 Dordogne memoir — the founding excavation record of Cro-Magnon man and palaeolithic cave life.

title: Völker, Rassen, Sprachen
creator: Felix von Luschan
description: Luschan's 1922 assault on race typology — the physical anthropologist who argued races were unstable human groupings, not fixed types.

title: On Pithecanthropus erectus
creator: Léonce Manouvrier
description: Manouvrier's 1897 critique — the Paris anthropologist's skeptical anatomical review of Dubois's Java ape-man.

title: The Jaw of the Piltdown Man
creator: Gerrit S. Miller Jr.
description: Miller's 1915 bombshell — the Smithsonian zoologist's demonstration that the Piltdown jaw was an ape's, the first great scientific challenge to the forgery.

title: Le Préhistorique: Antiquité de l'homme
creator: Gabriel de Mortillet
description: Mortillet's 1883 French synthesis — the classification of the Palaeolithic (Chellean, Mousterian, Solutrean, Magdalenian) still in use today.

title: Palaeolithic Man and Terramara Settlements in Europe
creator: Robert Munro
description: Munro's 1908 synthesis of palaeolithic man and the lake-dwellings — the bridge between deep antiquity and European prehistory.

title: Prehistoric Britain
creator: Robert Munro
description: Munro's 1913 Home University Library survey — the compact statement of the British palaeolithic case.

title: The Primitive Inhabitants of Scandinavia
creator: Sven Nilsson (translated by John Lubbock)
description: Nilsson's Scandinavian stone-age classic in Lubbock's 1868 translation — the northern counterpart to the French antiquity case.

title: Hesperopithecus, the First Anthropoid Primate Found in America
creator: Henry Fairfield Osborn
description: Osborn's April 1922 Novitates paper — the naming of 'Nebraska Man' from a single worn tooth, paleoanthropology's most famous false start.

title: Hesperopithecus, the Anthropoid Primate of Western Nebraska
creator: Henry Fairfield Osborn
description: Osborn's August 1922 Nature announcement of Hesperopithecus — the claim broadcast to the world before the tooth was re-examined.

title: Hesperopithecus, the First Anthropoid Primate Found in America
creator: Henry Fairfield Osborn
description: The National Academy version of Osborn's Hesperopithecus announcement, read April 25, 1922 — the 'Nebraska Man' claim at its most authoritative.

title: Antiquity of Man as Deduced from the Discovery of a Human Skeleton
creator: Richard Owen
description: Owen's 1884 verdict on the Tilbury Thames skeleton — the great comparative anatomist's late assessment of human antiquity.

title: On the Primitive Characters of the Flint Implements of the Chalk Plateau of Kent
creator: Joseph Prestwich
description: Prestwich's 1891 defense of Harrison's Kent eoliths — the great geologist staking his reputation on pre-glacial man, with the discussion in full.

title: De la mâchoire humaine de Moulin-Quignon: nouvelles découvertes
creator: Armand de Quatrefages
description: Quatrefages's 1864 Moulin-Quignon memoir — the French academy's defense of Boucher de Perthes's jaw as the controversy peaked.

title: Die Pithecanthropus-Schichten auf Java
creator: Emil Selenka and Max Blanckenhorn
description: The Selenka expedition's 1911 Java monograph — the first full geological and faunal re-study of Dubois's Trinil Pithecanthropus beds.

title: On the Discovery of Supposed Human Remains in the Tool-Bearing Drift of Moulin-Quignon
creator: Anonymous (Anthropological Review)
description: The English skeptics' 1863 broadside on the Moulin-Quignon jaw — the fraud-suspicion paper that forced the international congress.

title: Untersuchung des Neanderthal-Schädels
creator: Rudolf Virchow
description: Virchow's 1872 report on the Neanderthal skull — the pathological dismissal that held back acceptance of fossil man for decades.

title: Lectures on Man: His Place in Creation, and in the History of the Earth
creator: Carl Vogt (edited by James Hunt)
description: Vogt's 1864 English lectures — the most influential materialist synthesis of human origins before Darwin's Descent, arguing the ape-man case in full.

title: The Origin of Human Races and the Antiquity of Man Deduced from the Theory of 'Natural Selection'
creator: Alfred Russel Wallace
description: Wallace's 1864 paper — the first application of natural selection to human races and antiquity, and his first step toward the break with Darwin.

title: On the Origin of 'Eolithic' Flints by Natural Causes, Especially by the Foundering of Drifts
creator: S. Hazzledine Warren
description: Warren's 1905 natural-causes paper — the experimental demolition of the eoliths that ended the Tertiary-man debate in Britain.

title: Fourth Note on the Piltdown Gravel, with Evidence of a Second Skull of Eoanthropus dawsoni
creator: Arthur Smith Woodward (appendix by Grafton Elliot Smith)
description: Woodward's 1917 fourth Piltdown note — the 'second skull' (Piltdown II) that seemed to confirm Eoanthropus, with Elliot Smith's endocast appendix.

title: Man and the Glacial Period
creator: G. Frederick Wright
description: Wright's 1892 popular synthesis of man and the ice age — the American high-water mark of deep human antiquity before the backlash.

title: Mélusine
creator: Jean d'Arras
description: The Melusine archetype — the foundational fish-woman romance of 1393, in the 1895 Early English Text Society Middle English edition edited by A. K. Donald.

title: Curious Myths of the Middle Ages, Second Series
creator: Sabine Baring-Gould
description: The Victorian comparative survey of the Melusina legend (ch. VII), with chapters on swan-maidens and the Fortunate Isles — the standard 19th-century treatment; 1868 edition.

title: Journal of the First Voyage of Christopher Columbus
creator: Christopher Columbus
description: Columbus's 1493 mermaid sighting off the Rio del Oro — 'they were not as beautiful as they are said to be' — in Clements Markham's 1893 Hakluyt Society translation of the Las Casas abstract.

title: Henry Hudson the Navigator
creator: George M. Asher (ed.)
description: The Hakluyt Society edition of Hudson's journals, containing the 15 June 1608 mermaid sighting off Novaya Zemlya — the classic Arctic mermaid account, witnessed by Thomas Hilles and Robert Rayner.

title: Deux livres de chirurgie
creator: Ambroise Paré
description: First edition of Paré's two books of surgery; Book II is the 'Des monstres et prodiges' — the founding text of Renaissance teratology, with its chapter on marine monsters and the siren. In French.

title: Undine
creator: Friedrich de la Motte Fouqué
description: The literary codification of the undine — the water-spirit who wins a soul through marriage to a knight; the complete 19-chapter text in F. E. Bunnett's translation.

title: Northern Mythology, Vol. II
creator: Benjamin Thorpe
description: Vol. II of Thorpe's great collection of Northern popular traditions — Scandinavian merman and mermaid lore including 'The Merman and Mermaid'; completes the live Vol. I.

title: Northern Mythology, Vol. III
creator: Benjamin Thorpe
description: Vol. III of Thorpe's great collection of Northern popular traditions; completes the live Vol. I.

title: Teutonic Mythology, Vol. I
creator: Jacob Grimm (trans. James Steven Stallybrass)
description: Vol. I of Grimm's monumental mythology in Stallybrass's English translation — the authority on Germanic water-spirits, nixies, and sea-beings.

title: Teutonic Mythology, Vol. II
creator: Jacob Grimm (trans. James Steven Stallybrass)
description: Vol. II of Grimm's Teutonic Mythology in Stallybrass's translation.

title: Teutonic Mythology, Vol. III
creator: Jacob Grimm (trans. James Steven Stallybrass)
description: Vol. III of Grimm's Teutonic Mythology in Stallybrass's translation.

title: Teutonic Mythology, Vol. IV
creator: Jacob Grimm (trans. James Steven Stallybrass)
description: Vol. IV of Grimm's Teutonic Mythology in Stallybrass's translation (1888 printing).

title: Fairy Legends and Traditions of the South of Ireland
creator: Thomas Crofton Croker
description: The foundational Irish folklore collection — mermaid and merrow legends of the south of Ireland; 1844 Lea & Blanchard new edition.

title: Popular Romances of the West of England, First Series
creator: Robert Hunt
description: First series of Hunt's Cornish folklore — the Mermaid of Zennor and other sea-legends, drolls, and superstitions of old Cornwall.

title: Popular Romances of the West of England, Second Series
creator: Robert Hunt
description: Second series of Hunt's Cornish folklore — further drolls, traditions, and superstitions of old Cornwall; 1865 Hotten edition.

title: Celtic Fairy Tales
creator: Joseph Jacobs
description: The standard Victorian Celtic collection — includes 'The Sea-Maiden,' the Scottish mermaid tale.

title: More Celtic Fairy Tales
creator: Joseph Jacobs
description: Companion volume to Celtic Fairy Tales — further Celtic sea-maiden and water-spirit tales.

title: Fairy and Folk Tales of the Irish Peasantry
creator: W. B. Yeats (ed.)
description: Yeats's landmark anthology of Irish folklore — mermaid and merrow tales gathered from Croker, Carleton, and others.

title: Russian Fairy Tales
creator: W. R. S. Ralston
description: The foundational English collection of Russian folklore — rusalka (Slavic mermaid) tales and water-spirit lore.

title: Popular Tales of the West Highlands, Vol. I
creator: J. F. Campbell
description: Vol. I of the great Scottish Gaelic folklore collection, orally gathered in the Highlands — selkie and sea-maiden tales.

title: Popular Tales of the West Highlands, Vol. II
creator: J. F. Campbell
description: Vol. II of Campbell's West Highland tales.

title: Popular Tales of the West Highlands, Vol. III
creator: J. F. Campbell
description: Vol. III of Campbell's West Highland tales.

title: Popular Tales of the West Highlands, Vol. IV
creator: J. F. Campbell
description: Vol. IV of Campbell's West Highland tales.

title: Celtic Folklore: Welsh and Manx, Vol. I
creator: John Rhys
description: Vol. I of Rhys's Welsh and Manx folklore — the Manx ben-varrey (mermaid) and Welsh sea-legends.

title: Celtic Folklore: Welsh and Manx, Vol. II
creator: John Rhys
description: Vol. II of Rhys's Welsh and Manx folklore.

title: The Science of Fairy Tales
creator: Edwin Sidney Hartland
description: Pioneering folklore scholarship — the swan-maiden/Melusine tale-type traced across cultures.

title: Le Folk-lore des pêcheurs
creator: Paul Sébillot
description: The authority on French maritime folklore — sirènes, morgans, and sea-wonders of the Breton and Norman coasts. In French.

title: A House of Pomegranates
creator: Oscar Wilde
description: Contains 'The Fisherman and his Soul' — the great literary mermaid tale of the soulless sea-maiden.

title: The Humbugs of the World
creator: P. T. Barnum
description: Barnum's own account of the Feejee Mermaid — the manufactured Japanese ningyo exhibited as a veritable mermaid — and other humbugs.

title: A Wonderful Prophecy by a Mermaid
creator: Anonymous
description: Mermaid chapbook — John Robinson's six days adrift, the Whitehaven mermaid's prophecy, and his death five days after coming home; 1800 printing.

title: The Wonder of Wonders
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1795 Liverpool printing of the John Robinson mermaid-prophecy chapbook (cf. the 1800 Whitehaven printing) — a strange and wonderful relation of a mermaid seen and spoken with on the Black Rock.

title: Le Comte de Gabalis
creator: Abbé de Villars (Nicolas-Pierre-Henri de Montfaucon)
description: The Rosicrucian elemental romance that carried Paracelsus's nymphs and sylphs into 18th-century literature — Fouqué's direct source for Undine. In French; 1742 edition.

title: The Pentamerone
creator: Giambattista Basile (trans. John Edward Taylor)
description: The first European fairy-tale collection (1634-36) — sea-wonder tales including the Dolphin bridegroom; Taylor's 1850 English translation.

title: Sixty Folk-Tales from Exclusively Slavonic Sources
creator: A. H. Wratislaw
description: English collection of Slavonic folklore — Vila (water-nymph) tales including 'The Friendship of a Vila,' with mermaid parallels noted.

title: The Rise of the House of Rothschild
creator: Egon Caesar Corti (1886-1953), translated by Brian and Beatrix Lunn
description: Corti's The Rise of the House of Rothschild (New York: Blue Ribbon Books, 1928) — the documentary history of the family's rise, 1770-1830, drawn from family archives; the companion volume to the library's Reign (1830-1871). The serious scholarly history every later Rothschild study cites.

title: The Rothschilds: The Financial Rulers of Nations
creator: John Reeves
description: John Reeves's The Rothschilds: The Financial Rulers of Nations (Chicago: A. C. McClurg, 1887) — the first full-length English history of the banking house, cited in the Jewish Encyclopedia's Rothschild bibliography; a serious contemporary history, not polemic.

title: Das Haus Rothschild: Seine Geschichte und seine Geschäfte
creator: Friedrich Arnold Steinmann (1801-1875)
description: Friedrich Arnold Steinmann's Das Haus Rothschild (Prague, 1857; both parts) — the earliest serious German history of the house and its state finances, cited in the Jewish Encyclopedia bibliography; primary 19th-century scholarship.

title: Les Rothschild: une famille de financiers juifs au XIXe siècle
creator: Édouard Demachy
description: Édouard Demachy's Les Rothschild: une famille de financiers juifs au XIXe siècle (Paris, 1896) — a serious French documentary history of the family's nineteenth-century banking operations.

title: Les Juifs, rois de l'époque: histoire de la féodalité financière
creator: Alphonse Toussenel (1803-1885)
description: Alphonse Toussenel's Les Juifs, rois de l'époque (first published 1845; this complete 1888 edition) — the founding text of the 'féodalité financière' thesis that shaped all later Rothschild literature; pivotal in the history of economic antisemitism, hosted here strictly as a historical document.

title: Grand procès entre Rothschild Ier, roi des Juifs, et Satan, dernier roi des imposteurs
creator: Junius Grand (pseudonym)
description: The 1846 Paris pamphlet staging a mock 'trial' of Rothschild Ier against 'Satan' — a primary document of the pamphlet war that launched the Waterloo-profit legend; the press battle's satirical counter-voice, published the same year as Dairnvaell's origin pamphlet.

title: Dialogue aux enfers entre Machiavel et Montesquieu
creator: Maurice Joly (1829-1878)
description: Maurice Joly's Dialogue aux enfers entre Machiavel et Montesquieu (Brussels, 1864) — the complete 25-dialogue satire on Napoleon III that the Protocols of the Elders of Zion plagiarized; the foundation text of Philip Graves's 1921 exposure.

title: The Battle of Waterloo: Containing the Accounts Published by Authority, British and Foreign
creator: John Booth (publisher)
description: John Booth's The Battle of Waterloo (London, 1815) — the contemporary collection of the official British and foreign accounts of Waterloo as published in 1815; the published record the Rothschild 'early news' legend claims to have beaten, anchoring the legend's contemporary sources.

title: Das Rothschilder Lotterie-Anlehen von 20,800,000 Gulden
creator: Nikolaus Thaddäus Gönner (1764-1827)
description: Nikolaus Thaddäus Gönner's 1820 Munich legal dissertation on the Rothschild-Parish lottery loan of 20,800,000 gulden — contemporary legal literature on an early Rothschild sovereign loan; a primary document of the family's state-finance business.

title: Admission of Baron de Rothschild (Hansard, 26 July 1858)
creator: House of Commons (Hansard)
description: Hansard, HC Deb 26 July 1858, vol. 151, cc2105-15: the full Commons record of Baron Lionel de Rothschild's admission — sworn on the Old Testament after eleven years' exclusion — the climax of the Jewish emancipation struggle and the pivotal parliamentary record of the Rothschilds as MPs.

title: Supply — The Suez Canal Shares (Hansard, 14 February 1876)
creator: House of Commons (Hansard)
description: Hansard, HC Deb 14 February 1876, vol. 227, cc266-300: the Commons supply debate on the Suez Canal share purchase, recording on the parliamentary record that 'the Messrs. Rothschild undertook to pay' the Khedive £3,976,582 at 2.5% commission — the primary record of the Rothschild-financed purchase.

title: The Truth About "The Protocols": A Literary Forgery
creator: Philip Graves (1876-1953)
description: Philip Graves's The Truth About 'The Protocols': A Literary Forgery (London: The Times, 1921) — the three August 1921 Times articles exposing the Protocols as a plagiarism of Joly's Dialogue; the pivotal contemporary debunking, companion to the library's Protocols text.

title: Issue and Sale of Bonds: Report on the Rothschild-Morgan Bond Contract (1895)
creator: U.S. House of Representatives, Committee on Ways and Means
description: U.S. House Report No. 1824, 53rd Congress (13 February 1895): the congressional report printing the bond contract with the syndicate acting for N. M. Rothschild & Sons of London and J. P. Morgan & Co. — a primary published record of Rothschild sovereign lending, the 1895 U.S. gold-bond rescue.

title: The Balfour Declaration (1917)
creator: Arthur James Balfour (1848-1930)
description: Arthur Balfour's letter to Lord Rothschild, 2 November 1917 — the Balfour Declaration itself, addressed to Walter Rothschild for transmission to the Zionist Federation; the primary document of the family's most famous political moment.

title: Rothschild, Nathan Meyer (Dictionary of National Biography, 1897)
creator: Dictionary of National Biography
description: The Dictionary of National Biography, vol. 49 (1897): the DNB life of Nathan Mayer Rothschild, with subarticles on Sir Anthony de Rothschild and Meyer Amschel de Rothschild — serious scholarly biography from the standard Victorian reference work.

title: Rothschild, Lionel Nathan de (Dictionary of National Biography, 1897)
creator: Dictionary of National Biography
description: The Dictionary of National Biography, vol. 49 (1897): the DNB life of Lionel Nathan de Rothschild — the first professing Jew to sit in the Commons — serious scholarly biography from the standard Victorian reference work.

title: Rothschild, Ferdinand James de (Dictionary of National Biography, 1901)
creator: Thomas Seccombe (1866-1923)
description: The Dictionary of National Biography, 1901 supplement: Thomas Seccombe's DNB life of Ferdinand James de Rothschild — serious scholarly biography from the standard reference work.

title: Rothschild (The Jewish Encyclopedia, 1905)
creator: Joseph Jacobs, Isidore Singer, Frederick T. Haneman, Jacques Kahn, Goodman Lipkind, J. de Haas, et al.
description: The Jewish Encyclopedia (1905) 'Rothschild' article — the serious early-20th-century reference history of the family by Jacobs, Singer and colleagues, with a bibliography citing Steinmann (1857) and Reeves (1887); the scholarly baseline for the whole cluster.

title: A Beleaguered City
creator: Margaret Oliphant
description: Oliphant's novella of a French town besieged by its own dead — a siege-ghost story of rare strangeness and gravity.

title: A Strange Story
creator: Edward Bulwer-Lytton
description: Bulwer-Lytton's occult romance of mesmerism, alchemy, and the elixir of life — the Victorian occult novel's great popular success.

title: Allan Quatermain
creator: H. Rider Haggard
description: Quatermain's last journey into the unknown — the sequel that deepens Haggard's adventurer into myth.

title: Ayesha: The Return of She
creator: H. Rider Haggard
description: The Return of She — Ayesha's reincarnation saga continued; Haggard's occult romance at full stretch.

title: Carmilla
creator: Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu
description: The seminal lesbian vampire novella — predating Dracula by 26 years and establishing the female vampire archetype. A pivotal weird-fiction first.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
creator: Oscar Wilde
description: The original 13-chapter Lippincott's magazine text of Dorian Gray — rawer and more scandalous than the 1891 book; a distinct edition of a pivotal novel, transcribed from the July 1890 page scans.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
creator: Oscar Wilde
description: Wilde's only novel in its expanded book form — the Faustian portrait, aestheticism's dark masterpiece, with added chapters and the famous preface.

title: Dracula
creator: Bram Stoker
description: The novel that codified the vampire for the modern imagination — Count Dracula, Van Helsing, and the epistolary Gothic at full power. The pivotal vampire text.

title: Dracula's Guest and Other Weird Stories
creator: Bram Stoker
description: Posthumous collection of Stoker's weird tales, opening with the excised first chapter of Dracula — essential Stoker supernatural short fiction.

title: Erewhon
creator: Samuel Butler
description: Butler's satirical utopia — machines outlawed, illness criminalized; Victorian speculative fiction's sharpest satire.

title: Frankenstein; Or, The Modern Prometheus
creator: Mary Shelley
description: The 1818 first text of Frankenstein — the first science-fiction novel, in its original anonymous three-volume form.

title: Frankenstein; Or, The Modern Prometheus
creator: Mary Shelley
description: Shelley's revised 1831 Frankenstein — the standard text most readers know, with her new introduction and the reworked frame.

title: Grim Tales
creator: E. Nesbit
description: Nesbit's horror collection — 'Man-Size in Marble' and other tales of marital dread; the children's fantasist's dark double.

title: Hauntings: Fantastic Stories
creator: Vernon Lee
description: Vernon Lee's 'fantastic stories' — 'Oke of Okehurst,' 'A Wicked Voice'; aesthetic-decadent ghost fiction of the first rank.

title: In a Glass Darkly
creator: Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu
description: Five tales of the occult detective Dr. Hesselius, including 'Green Tea' and 'Carmilla' — the founding collection of the psychic-detective story. Assembled from the three-volume Project Gutenberg edition.

title: Island Nights' Entertainments
creator: Robert Louis Stevenson
description: Three South Seas tales including 'The Bottle Imp' — Stevenson's Pacific supernatural fiction, among his most perfectly made stories.

title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
creator: Robert Louis Stevenson
description: The defining Victorian tale of the double — Stevenson's chemical fable of duality that made 'Jekyll and Hyde' permanent cultural shorthand.

title: The Jewel of Seven Stars
creator: Bram Stoker
description: Stoker's Egyptian-revival mummy novel — an ancient queen's resurrection in Edwardian London, among the founding texts of mummy horror.

title: Khaled: A Tale of Arabia
creator: F. Marion Crawford
description: Crawford's Arabian Nights tale of a genie who becomes human for love — Orientalist fantasy by the era's most cosmopolitan romancer.

title: King Solomon's Mines
creator: H. Rider Haggard
description: The book that invented the lost-world adventure — Allan Quatermain's quest for the diamond mines; the template for a century of thrillers.

title: The Lair of the White Worm
creator: Bram Stoker
description: Stoker's final novel — a Lancashire legend of a giant worm-goddess; weird fiction at its most feverish and strange.

title: Lilith
creator: George MacDonald
description: MacDonald's dark adult fantasy of the shadow-world — a dream-vision of death and redemption, standing with Phantastes as his masterpiece.

title: Looking Backward: 2000–1887
creator: Edward Bellamy
description: Bellamy's utopian blockbuster — the sleeper wakes in the year 2000; among the best-selling American novels of the century's second half.

title: Lord Arthur Savile's Crime and Other Stories
creator: Oscar Wilde
description: Wilde's comic-crime collection — 'Lord Arthur Savile's Crime,' 'The Canterville Ghost,' and others; the ghost story turned inside out.

title: Lot No. 249
creator: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Doyle's mummy story — a revived Egyptian priest stalks Oxford; the founding text of mummy horror alongside Stoker's Jewel. Extracted complete from a Doyle weird-tales collection.

title: Markheim
creator: Robert Louis Stevenson
