title: Shakespeare's Sonnets
creator: William Shakespeare
description: The 1609 first-edition sequence of 154 sonnets — the most famous sonnet cycle in English.

title: Hamlet
creator: William Shakespeare
description: The most performed play in world literature — the tragedy of the Prince of Denmark, first printed 1603, in the standard reading text.

title: Macbeth
creator: William Shakespeare
description: Shakespeare's great tragedy of ambition and guilt, first printed in the 1623 First Folio, in the standard reading text.

title: Othello
creator: William Shakespeare
description: The tragedy of jealousy and manipulation, first printed 1622, in the standard reading text.

title: King Lear
creator: William Shakespeare
description: Shakespeare's bleakest tragedy — madness, ingratitude, and the gods — first printed 1608, in the standard reading text.

title: Romeo and Juliet
creator: William Shakespeare
description: The archetypal tragedy of young love, first printed 1597, in the standard reading text.

title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
creator: William Shakespeare
description: Shakespeare's most beloved comedy of lovers, fairies, and rude mechanicals, first printed 1600, in the standard reading text.

title: The Tempest
creator: William Shakespeare
description: Shakespeare's final solo play — Prospero's island of magic and forgiveness — first printed in the 1623 First Folio.

title: Paradise Lost
creator: John Milton
description: The great English epic — Satan, Adam, and the Fall — in the 1667 first-edition text.

title: Paradise Regained
creator: John Milton
description: Milton's brief epic on the temptation of Christ in the wilderness, in the 1671 first-edition text.

title: Samson Agonistes
creator: John Milton
description: Milton's closet tragedy on the blinded Samson, published with Paradise Regained in 1671; text from H. C. Beeching's landmark Oxford edition of Milton's poetical works (1900).

title: L'Allegro, Il Penseroso, Comus, and Lycidas
creator: John Milton
description: Milton's great masque Comus (performed 1634) with his essential early poems — the classic minor-poems volume.

title: The Canterbury Tales, and Other Poems
creator: Geoffrey Chaucer
description: The complete Tales in Middle English, in D. Laing Purves's standard edition — the founding work of English literature.

title: Faust: A Tragedy, Part 1
creator: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, translated by Bayard Taylor
description: Bayard Taylor's 1870 translation in the original metres — the landmark American Faust that made Goethe's masterpiece an English classic.

title: Faust: A Tragedy, Part 2
creator: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, translated by Bayard Taylor
description: Taylor's 1871 completion of his metrical translation — the first great English rendering of Faust's second part, from the first-edition Osgood printing.

title: Moby Dick; Or, The Whale
creator: Herman Melville
description: The great American novel — Ahab, Ishmael, and the white whale — in the 1851 first American edition text.

title: Billy Budd
creator: Herman Melville
description: Melville's posthumous novella, first published 1924 — his final meditation on justice, innocence, and martial law.

title: Leaves of Grass (1855 first edition)
creator: Walt Whitman
description: The 1855 Brooklyn first edition — twelve untitled poems, self-published and self-reviewed — the most famous first edition in American poetry.

title: Gulliver's Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World
creator: Jonathan Swift
description: The great voyage satire — Lilliput to the Houyhnhnms — in the 1726 first-edition text.

title: Pride and Prejudice
creator: Jane Austen
description: Austen's most beloved novel — Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy — in the 1813 first-edition text.

title: Sense and Sensibility
creator: Jane Austen
description: Austen's first published novel (1811) — the Dashwood sisters, sense against sensibility.

title: Emma
creator: Jane Austen
description: Austen's great comedy of self-deception — 'handsome, clever, and rich' Emma Woodhouse — in the 1815 text.

title: Persuasion
creator: Jane Austen
description: Austen's posthumous final novel (1817) — Anne Elliot's quiet, autumnal second chance at love.

title: Mansfield Park
creator: Jane Austen
description: Austen's most morally serious novel — Fanny Price at Mansfield — in the 1814 text.

title: Northanger Abbey
creator: Jane Austen
description: Austen's posthumous Gothic parody (1817) — Catherine Morland's imagination runs wild.

title: Oliver Twist
creator: Charles Dickens
description: Dickens's great novel of the workhouse and the London underworld, in the 1838 text.

title: A Christmas Carol
creator: Charles Dickens
description: The immortal ghost story of Scrooge's redemption, in the 1843 first-edition text.

title: David Copperfield
creator: Charles Dickens
description: Dickens's most autobiographical novel — 'my favourite child' — in the 1850 text.

title: Bleak House
creator: Charles Dickens
description: The great Chancery novel — Jarndyce v. Jarndyce — in the 1853 text.

title: Great Expectations
creator: Charles Dickens
description: Pip, Miss Havisham, and the convict Magwitch — Dickens's perfect late novel, in the 1861 text.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
creator: Charles Dickens
description: 'It was the best of times' — the French Revolution novel, in the 1859 text.

title: Crime and Punishment
creator: Fyodor Dostoevsky, translated by Constance Garnett
description: Constance Garnett's 1914 translation — the landmark rendering that introduced Dostoevsky to the English-speaking world.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
creator: Fyodor Dostoevsky, translated by Constance Garnett
description: Garnett's 1912 translation of Dostoevsky's final novel — the landmark English Karamazov.

title: The Idiot
creator: Fyodor Dostoevsky, translated by Eva Martin
description: Eva Martin's 1915 translation for J.M. Dent — the early Everyman-era English Idiot, Prince Myshkin's tragedy of goodness.

title: Notes from the Underground
creator: Fyodor Dostoevsky, translated by Constance Garnett
description: Garnett's translation of the founding text of existentialist fiction — the Underground Man's revolt against reason.

title: Les Misérables
creator: Victor Hugo, translated by Isabel Florence Hapgood
description: Isabel Hapgood's 1887 translation — the landmark complete English Les Misérables, still the standard public-domain rendering.

title: Notre-Dame de Paris
creator: Victor Hugo, translated by Isabel Florence Hapgood
description: Hapgood's 1888 translation of Hugo's great Gothic novel of medieval Paris — Quasimodo and Esmeralda.

title: Father Goriot
creator: Honoré de Balzac, translated by Ellen Marriage
description: Ellen Marriage's translation for J.M. Dent's landmark complete Comédie Humaine — the great novel of Parisian ambition.

title: Eugénie Grandet
creator: Honoré de Balzac, translated by Katharine Prescott Wormeley
description: Katharine Prescott Wormeley's translation, from her pioneering American Balzac series — the great provincial novel of miserliness and thwarted love.

title: Cousin Betty
creator: Honoré de Balzac, translated by James Waring
description: James Waring's 1888 translation — the FIRST English translation of Balzac's dark masterpiece of envy and revenge.

title: War and Peace
creator: Leo Tolstoy, translated by Aylmer Maude
description: Aylmer Maude's Oxford translation — the landmark English War and Peace, made in consultation with Tolstoy's own circle.

title: Anna Karenina
creator: Leo Tolstoy, translated by Constance Garnett
description: Garnett's 1901 translation — the first major English Anna Karenina, the rendering that made Tolstoy's novel an English classic.

title: Madame Bovary
creator: Gustave Flaubert, translated by Eleanor Marx Aveling
description: Eleanor Marx-Aveling's 1886 translation — the FIRST English translation of the founding novel of literary realism.

title: Salammbô
creator: Gustave Flaubert, translated by J. S. Chartres
description: J. S. Chartres's 1886 translation (J.M. Dent edition) of Flaubert's great Carthaginian epic of the Mercenary Revolt.

title: Germinal
creator: Émile Zola, translated by Havelock Ellis
description: Havelock Ellis's 1894 translation — the landmark English Germinal, Zola's great novel of the mining strike.

title: A Doll's House: A Play
creator: Henrik Ibsen, translated by R. Farquharson Sharp
description: R. Farquharson Sharp's 1911 Dent translation of the play that detonated modern drama — Nora's door-slam heard round the world.

title: Hedda Gabler
creator: Henrik Ibsen, translated by William Archer
description: William Archer's 1891 translation — from the critic who introduced Ibsen to England — of Ibsen's most dangerous heroine.

title: Ghosts
creator: Henrik Ibsen, translated by William Archer
description: Archer's 1890 translation of the play that scandalized London — heredity, hypocrisy, and the sins of the fathers.

title: Plays by Anton Chekhov, Second Series
creator: Anton Chekhov, translated by Julius West
description: Julius West's 1916 volume containing The Three Sisters and The Cherry Orchard — Chekhov's two greatest plays in early English dress.

title: The Raven
creator: Edgar Allan Poe
description: The poem that made Poe famous, first published 1845 — the most famous American poem of the 19th century.

title: The Works of Edgar Allan Poe, The Raven Edition
creator: Edgar Allan Poe
description: The landmark Stedman-Woodberry Raven Edition (1902-03) — the first scholarly complete Poe; this volume gathers the great tales and the Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym.

title: De Profundis
creator: Oscar Wilde
description: Wilde's prison letter to Lord Alfred Douglas, first published 1905 — the essential Wilde document.

title: The Importance of Being Earnest: A Trivial Comedy for Serious People
creator: Oscar Wilde
description: The greatest comedy in English — first published 1899, four years after its triumphant premiere.

title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
creator: Mark Twain
description: The great American novel, COMPLETE — Huck and Jim on the Mississippi — in the 1884 first-edition text.

title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
creator: Mark Twain
description: The beloved Mississippi boyhood novel, complete, in the 1876 first-edition text.

title: The Iliad
creator: Homer, translated by George Chapman
description: Chapman's 1616 Iliad — the first complete English Iliad, the translation Keats celebrated.

title: The Iliad
creator: Homer, translated by Alexander Pope
description: Pope's 1715-20 Iliad — the great Augustan Iliad, the most famous English Homer.

title: The Odyssey
creator: Homer, translated by George Chapman
description: Chapman's 1615 Odyssey — the first complete English Odyssey.

title: The Odyssey
creator: Homer, translated by Alexander Pope
description: Pope's 1725-26 Odyssey — the Augustan companion to his Iliad.

title: The Prince
creator: Niccolò Machiavelli, translated by Edward Dacres
description: Dacres's 1640 Prince — the first English translation of Machiavelli's masterpiece.

title: Meditations
creator: Marcus Aurelius, translated by Meric Casaubon
description: Casaubon's 1634 Meditations — the first English Marcus Aurelius.

title: Metamorphoses
creator: Ovid, translated by Arthur Golding
description: Golding's 1567 Metamorphoses — the first English Ovid, Shakespeare's Ovid, the most influential Elizabethan translation.

title: Pseudomonarchia Daemonum
creator: Johann Weyer, Englished by Reginald Scot
description: Scot's 1584 English Pseudomonarchia — the first English text of Weyer's demonology, from the Discoverie of Witchcraft.

title: History of the Peloponnesian War
creator: Thucydides, translated by Thomas Hobbes
description: Hobbes's 1629 Thucydides — the first English Thucydides translated from Greek, by the author of Leviathan.

title: Jane Eyre
creator: Charlotte Brontë
description: The foundational Victorian bildungsroman and the defining first-person narrative of female independence; the novel every later 'governess novel' and feminist bildungsroman answers to.

title: Shirley
creator: Charlotte Brontë
description: Brontë's ambitious 'condition of England' novel, set against the Luddite risings; the first major industrial novel by a woman.

title: Villette
creator: Charlotte Brontë
description: Brontë's most psychologically intricate novel; a landmark of interior narrative and unconsummated desire that anticipates modernism.

title: The Professor
creator: Charlotte Brontë
description: Brontë's first-written, posthumously published novel; the seedbed of Villette and Jane Eyre, essential for understanding her development.

title: Wuthering Heights
creator: Emily Brontë
description: The most radical novel of the Victorian era — a storm-driven metaphysical romance that broke every convention of the realist novel.

title: Agnes Grey
creator: Anne Brontë
description: Anne Brontë's quietly devastating governess novel; the first novel to expose the governess's economic and social humiliation from the inside.

title: The Tenant of Wildfell Hall
creator: Anne Brontë
description: A shocking exposé of marital abuse and alcoholism; the first feminist novel to argue a wife's right to leave a destructive marriage.

title: Poems by Currer, Ellis, and Acton Bell
creator: Charlotte Brontë, Emily Brontë, Anne Brontë
description: The Brontës' 1846 debut as Currer, Ellis, and Acton Bell, plus selections from their literary remains — the launch of three literary careers.

title: The Life of Charlotte Brontë
creator: Elizabeth Gaskell
description: The first great modern literary biography — by a fellow novelist and friend — which single-handedly created the Brontë myth. Staged complete: both volumes combined.

title: The Three Musketeers
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: The archetypal swashbuckler and the most beloved adventure novel ever written; the founding text of the historical adventure genre.

title: Twenty Years After
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: The middle volume of the d'Artagnan romances, set during the Fronde; the first great sequel that deepened rather than repeated its predecessor.

title: The Vicomte de Bragelonne
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: The opening section of the final d'Artagnan romance (chapters 1–75): Raoul de Bragelonne's tragedy begins as the musketeers age into legend.

title: Ten Years Later
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: The second section of the final d'Artagnan romance (chapters 76–140): court intrigue, Fouquet's fall, and the gathering of the Iron Mask mystery.

title: Louise de la Valliere
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: The third section of the final d'Artagnan romance (chapters 141–208): Louis XIV's passion and Raoul's doom.

title: The Man in the Iron Mask
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: The immortal conclusion of the d'Artagnan romances (chapters 209–269): the mystery of the masked prisoner and the death of the musketeers.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: The ultimate revenge novel — Edmond Dantès' transformation into the Count of Monte Cristo; the most plotted novel in literature.

title: The Black Tulip
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: Dumas's Dutch historical romance of the tulip mania — a jewel-like miniature of his art, pairing political intrigue with horticultural obsession.

title: The Corsican Brothers
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: Dumas's eerie Corsican vendetta tale in Henry Frith's translation — the definitive literary treatment of the Corsican blood-feud.

title: Marguerite de Valois
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: Dumas's great Valois romance of the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre — the first volume of his Wars of Religion trilogy.

title: Chicot the Jester
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: The classic abridged English version of La dame de Monsoreau (1846), Dumas's beloved romance of Henri III's court — the Valois trilogy's middle volume.

title: The Forty-Five Guardsmen
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: The conclusion of the Valois trilogy — Henri III's forty-five Gascon guards against the Guise faction; Dumas at his most cinematic.

title: The Queen's Necklace
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: Dumas's romance of the Diamond Necklace Affair — the scandal that doomed Marie Antoinette; second of the Marie Antoinette romances.

title: The Regent's Daughter
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: Dumas's romance of the Cellamare conspiracy against the Regent Philippe d'Orléans — the opening of his Regency cycle.

title: The Companions of Jehu
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: Dumas's romance of the royalist Companions of Jehu under the Directory — highwaymen, secret societies, and Napoleon's rise.

title: The Chevalier de Maison-Rouge
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: Dumas's romance of the Chevalier de Rougeville's plot to save Marie Antoinette — the Terror's most thrilling adventure.

title: Georges
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: Dumas's novel of a mixed-race hero returning to Mauritius to confront slavery and racism — a pioneering abolitionist romance (staged in the French original).

title: The Whites and the Blues
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: Dumas's late Napoleonic epic — royalists (Whites) versus republicans (Blues) from Valmy to the Consulate; his last great historical panorama.

title: The Countess of Charny
creator: Alexandre Dumas
description: The culmination of the Marie Antoinette romances — the Revolution's climax and the execution of Louis XVI, in Henry Llewellyn Williams' translation.

title: Robinson Crusoe
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: The first English novel in the modern sense; invented realist fiction, the castaway narrative, and the economic individual as hero.

title: Moll Flanders
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: The great criminal autobiography of English fiction; the founding picaresque of the modern novel.

title: A Journal of the Plague Year
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: The pseudo-documentary of the 1665 London plague; invented the documentary novel and disaster reportage.

title: Memoirs of a Cavalier
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: Defoe's military memoir of the Thirty Years' War and English Civil War — the founding historical novel in English.

title: An Essay upon Projects
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: Defoe's prospectus for social reform — banks, insurance, academies for women; the founding document of the project literature.

title: Roxana
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: Defoe's last and darkest novel — the 'Fortunate Mistress' and her moral collapse; the first novel of bourgeois guilt.

title: Colonel Jack
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: The criminal-to-gentleman arc of Colonel Jack; Defoe's great novel of social mobility and reformation.

title: Captain Singleton
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: Defoe's pirate novel — the crossing of Africa and the pirate republic; the source-text of pirate literature.

title: The Storm
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: Defoe's eyewitness collection on the Great Storm of 1703; the first work of modern journalism.

title: A General History of the Pyrates
creator: Charles Johnson
description: Published under the name 'Captain Charles Johnson' and long attributed to Defoe; the history of Blackbeard, Bartholomew Roberts, and the golden age of piracy — the source of nearly every pirate myth.

title: The True-Born Englishman
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: Defoe's bestselling verse satire defending William III — 'we are really all foreigners ourselves'; the first great poem of English multiculturalism.

title: The Consolidator
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: Defoe's satirical voyage to the Moon — a lunar parliament debating English politics; one of the first science-fiction satires in English.

title: A New Voyage Round the World
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: Defoe's last great adventure novel — a merchant voyage round the globe by a course never sailed before; the mature statement of his travel fiction.

title: The Scarlet Letter
creator: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: The great American novel of guilt and Puritan conscience; the founding text of American psychological fiction.

title: The House of the Seven Gables
creator: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: The romance of the Pyncheon curse and inherited guilt; Hawthorne's great novel of American class and decay.

title: The Blithedale Romance
creator: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: The Brook Farm roman à clef; the first great American novel of utopian community and its discontents.

title: The Marble Faun
creator: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: The last completed romance — Rome, art, and the Fall; the novel Henry James called the bridge to the international theme.

title: Twice-Told Tales
creator: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: The complete story collection that made Hawthorne's name; the founding book of the American short story.

title: A Wonder-Book for Girls and Boys
creator: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: The retold Greek myths for children; the book that fixed the classical myths in the Anglophone imagination.

title: Tanglewood Tales
creator: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: The second volume of retold Greek myths; with A Wonder-Book, the canon of children's classical mythology.

title: Fanshawe
creator: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: Hawthorne's first, suppressed novel — a college romance he tried to destroy; essential to the Hawthorne canon's origins.

title: The Snow-Image, and Other Twice-Told Tales
creator: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: The complete collection 'The Snow-Image, and Other Twice-Told Tales' — including 'The Great Stone Face' and 'Ethan Brand'.

title: Our Old Home
creator: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: Hawthorne's English sketches from his Liverpool consulship — the great American writer's reckoning with England.

title: The Whole History of Grandfather's Chair
creator: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: 'The Whole History of Grandfather's Chair' — Hawthorne's New England history for children, from the Puritans to the Revolution.

title: Nature
creator: Ralph Waldo Emerson
description: The slim book that launched transcendentalism; the founding text of American nature writing.

title: Essays: First Series
creator: Ralph Waldo Emerson
description: Contains 'Self-Reliance' and 'The Over-Soul'; the founding document of American intellectual independence.

title: Essays: Second Series
creator: Ralph Waldo Emerson
description: Contains 'The Poet' and 'Experience'; the mature statement of transcendentalist aesthetics.

title: Representative Men
creator: Ralph Waldo Emerson
description: The lectures on Plato, Shakespeare, Goethe, and Napoleon; the great 19th-century theory of genius and heroism.

title: The Conduct of Life
creator: Ralph Waldo Emerson
description: The late essays on fate, power, wealth, and culture; Emerson's practical philosophy at its most aphoristic.

title: English Traits
creator: Ralph Waldo Emerson
description: The travel-book on England; the first great American comparative study of national character.

title: Poems (Emerson, 1847)
creator: Ralph Waldo Emerson
description: The collected poems including 'Concord Hymn' and 'The Rhodora'; the verse counterpart to the essays.

title: Society and Solitude
creator: Ralph Waldo Emerson
description: The late essay collection — 'Society and Solitude', 'Civilization', 'Art', 'Eloquence'; Emerson's final summing-up.

title: Letters and Social Aims
creator: Ralph Waldo Emerson
description: The final lifetime collection — 'Poetry and Imagination', 'The Comic', 'Quotation and Originality', 'Immortality'.

title: Walden
creator: Henry David Thoreau
description: The experiment in deliberate living; the founding text of environmental thought and simple-living philosophy.

title: Civil Disobedience
creator: Henry David Thoreau
description: The essay on the duty to resist unjust government; the charter of nonviolent civil disobedience.

title: A Week on the Concord and Merrimack Rivers
creator: Henry David Thoreau
description: Thoreau's first book — the river journey with his brother; the elegy that contains the seed of Walden.

title: The Maine Woods
creator: Henry David Thoreau
description: The posthumous wilderness narratives; the founding text of American wilderness writing.

title: Cape Cod
creator: Henry David Thoreau
description: The posthumous Cape Cod travel narrative; the great American book of the sea-shore.

title: Excursions
creator: Henry David Thoreau
description: The posthumous essay collection containing 'Walking' — the manifesto of the saunter and wildness.

title: A Plea for Captain John Brown
creator: Henry David Thoreau
description: Thoreau's thunderous defense of John Brown after Harpers Ferry — the most radical abolitionist address of the era.

title: A Yankee in Canada, with Anti-Slavery and Reform Papers
creator: Henry David Thoreau
description: The 1866 posthumous collection — 'A Yankee in Canada' plus the Anti-Slavery and Reform Papers ('Slavery in Massachusetts', 'Life Without Principle', 'Wendell Phillips').

title: The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman
creator: Laurence Sterne
description: The most formally radical novel of the 18th century — digression, blank pages, marbled pages, and metafiction a century before modernism. Complete nine books (Everyman's Library edition).

title: A Sentimental Journey Through France and Italy
creator: Laurence Sterne
description: The unfinished travel narrative that named sensibility; the founding text of sentimental travel literature.

title: The Road to Damascus
creator: August Strindberg
description: The great trilogy of the Inferno crisis — the soul's journey through guilt and conversion; the bridge from naturalism to expressionism, in Graham Rawson's translation.

title: Inferno
creator: August Strindberg
description: The autobiographical record of Strindberg's occult crisis in Paris — paranoia, alchemy, and spiritual breakdown, in Claud Field's 1913 translation.

title: The Red Room
creator: August Strindberg
description: The novel that made Strindberg famous — the first modern Swedish novel, a satirical panorama of Stockholm's artistic underworld, in Ellie Schleussner's 1913 translation.

title: Married
creator: August Strindberg
description: The story collection that got Strindberg prosecuted for blasphemy — twenty tales of marriage as war; the scandal-book of 1880s Scandinavia.

title: Master Olof
creator: August Strindberg
description: Strindberg's breakthrough historical drama of Olaus Petri and the Swedish Reformation, in Edwin Björkman's translation — the play of his youth.

title: Lucky Pehr
creator: August Strindberg
description: The allegorical five-act fairy play of Pehr's journey, in Velma Swanston Howard's authorized translation — Strindberg's most performed early play.

title: Candide (First English Translation, 1760)
creator: Voltaire
description: Anonymous first English translation ('Candidus; or, All for the Best,' London: M. Cooper, 1760), predating Smollett's; includes the spurious contemporary Part II as published.

title: The Mathnawi of Jalalu'ddin Rumi, Vol. VI (Nicholson Translation)
creator: Reynold A. Nicholson
description: Nicholson's landmark English translation of Rumi's Mathnawi, Books V-VI (E.J.W. Gibb Memorial, 1934); completes the library's Mathnawi translation set. US public domain: no copyright renewal found in the 1962 Catalog of Copyright Entries.

title: A Tour thro' the Whole Island of Great Britain
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: Defoe's pioneering work of travel writing and social observation; the first comprehensive survey of Britain's economy and society before the Industrial Revolution.

title: The Shortest Way with the Dissenters
creator: Daniel Defoe
description: Defoe's savage ironic pamphlet urging persecution of Dissenters; taken literally, it led to his prosecution, pillorying, and ruin in 1703.

title: History of Greece, Vol. 1 (Murray, 1888)
creator: George Grote
description: Volume 1 of Grote's monumental History of Greece (John Murray, 1888 ten-volume edition) — the foundational modern history of ancient Greece.

title: History of Greece, Vol. 2 (Murray, 1888)
creator: George Grote
description: Volume 2 of Grote's monumental History of Greece (John Murray, 1888 ten-volume edition) — the foundational modern history of ancient Greece.

title: History of Greece, Vol. 3 (Murray, 1888)
creator: George Grote
description: Volume 3 of Grote's monumental History of Greece (John Murray, 1888 ten-volume edition) — the foundational modern history of ancient Greece.

title: History of Greece, Vol. 4 (Murray, 1888)
creator: George Grote
description: Volume 4 of Grote's monumental History of Greece (John Murray, 1888 ten-volume edition) — the foundational modern history of ancient Greece.

title: History of Greece, Vol. 5 (Murray, 1888)
creator: George Grote
description: Volume 5 of Grote's monumental History of Greece (John Murray, 1888 ten-volume edition) — the foundational modern history of ancient Greece.

title: History of Greece, Vol. 6 (Murray, 1888)
creator: George Grote
description: Volume 6 of Grote's monumental History of Greece (John Murray, 1888 ten-volume edition) — the foundational modern history of ancient Greece.

title: History of Greece, Vol. 7 (Murray, 1888)
creator: George Grote
description: Volume 7 of Grote's monumental History of Greece (John Murray, 1888 ten-volume edition) — the foundational modern history of ancient Greece.

title: History of Greece, Vol. 8 (Murray, 1888)
creator: George Grote
description: Volume 8 of Grote's monumental History of Greece (John Murray, 1888 ten-volume edition) — the foundational modern history of ancient Greece.

title: History of Greece, Vol. 9 (Murray, 1888)
creator: George Grote
description: Volume 9 of Grote's monumental History of Greece (John Murray, 1888 ten-volume edition) — the foundational modern history of ancient Greece.

title: History of Greece, Vol. 10 (Murray, 1888)
creator: George Grote
description: Volume 10 of Grote's monumental History of Greece (John Murray, 1888 ten-volume edition) — the foundational modern history of ancient Greece.

title: The Father
creator: August Strindberg
description: The naturalist tragedy of the Captain's destruction in the battle of the sexes — the play that made Strindberg world-famous, in Edith and Warner Oland's translation.

title: Miss Julie
creator: August Strindberg
description: The one-act naturalist tragedy of Midsummer Eve — the most performed Strindberg play in the world, in the Olands' translation ('Countess Julie').

title: The Outlaw
creator: August Strindberg
description: The early one-act Viking tragedy — Strindberg's first produced play, in the Olands' translation.

title: The Stronger
creator: August Strindberg
description: The ten-minute one-woman duel of two actresses — the most perfect miniature in modern drama, in the Olands' translation.

title: Comrades
creator: August Strindberg

title: The Chinese Classics, Vol. 4, Part 2: The She King (Book of Poetry)
creator: James Legge (trans.)
description: Completes Legge's She King (Vol. 4 Part 1 live) — the first English translation of the Classic of Poetry. Full text, public domain.

title: The Chinese Classics, Vol. 5, Part 1: The Ch'un Ts'ew (Spring and Autumn Annals)
creator: James Legge (trans.)
description: Vol. 5 Part 1 of Legge's Chinese Classics — the first English translation of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Full text, public domain.

title: The Chinese Classics, Vol. 5, Part 2: The Ch'un Ts'ew (Spring and Autumn Annals)
creator: James Legge (trans.)
description: Vol. 5 Part 2 of Legge's Chinese Classics. Full text, public domain.

title: The Sacred Books of the East, Vol. 3: The Shû King (The Sacred Books of China, Part 1)
creator: James Legge (trans.)
description: One of two missing SBE volumes (of 50) — brings the library's Sacred Books of the East to 49/50. Full text, public domain.

title: The Sacred Books of the East, Vol. 36: The Questions of King Milinda, Part 2
creator: T. W. Rhys Davids (trans.)
description: The last missing SBE volume — completes the 50-volume Sacred Books of the East (Part 1 live). Full text, public domain.

title: Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy (Motte translation, 1729)
creator: Isaac Newton (Andrew Motte, trans.)
description: First English translation of the Principia — the text by which Newton entered the English-speaking world. Full text, public domain.

title: Opticks: Or, A Treatise of the Reflections, Refractions, Inflections and Colours of Light
creator: Isaac Newton
description: First edition of the founding work of physical optics — absent from the library. Full text, public domain.

title: Dialogues Concerning Two New Sciences
creator: Galileo Galilei (Henry Crew and Alfonso de Salvio, trans.)
description: Landmark English translation of Galileo's final masterpiece — the founding text of modern physics, absent from the library. Full text, public domain.

title: Treatise on Light
creator: Christiaan Huygens (Silvanus P. Thompson, trans.)
description: First English translation of the founding text of wave optics (orig. 1690). Full text, public domain.

title: A New System of Chemical Philosophy, Part 1
creator: John Dalton
description: First statement of the modern atomic theory — the founding document of modern chemistry, absent from the library. Full text, public domain.

title: Micrographia
creator: Robert Hooke
description: First major work of microscopy; coined the term 'cell' — absent from the library. Full text, public domain.

title: The Chemical History of a Candle
creator: Michael Faraday
description: The landmark of popular science — Faraday's Royal Institution Christmas lectures. Full text, public domain.

title: An Essay on Crimes and Punishments
creator: Cesare Beccaria
description: First English edition (1767) of the founding text of criminology and penal reform. Full text, public domain.

title: The Positive Philosophy of Auguste Comte, Vol. 2
creator: Auguste Comte (Harriet Martineau, trans.)
description: Vol. 2 of Martineau's landmark translation - completes the English Positive Philosophy. Full text, public domain.

title: The Essence of Christianity
creator: Ludwig Feuerbach (George Eliot, trans.)
description: George Eliot's landmark translation — the work that shaped Victorian religious thought. Full text, public domain.

title: The Life of Jesus Critically Examined
creator: David Friedrich Strauss (George Eliot, trans.)
description: George Eliot's first book-length translation — the landmark English Strauss that launched the Victorian crisis of faith. Full text, public domain.

title: The Monadology and Other Philosophical Writings
creator: G. W. Leibniz (Robert Latta, trans.)
description: Latta's landmark English edition of the Monadology — the standard English Leibniz for a generation. Full text, public domain.

title: An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding
creator: David Hume
description: Hume's mature statement of empiricism — a major work absent from the library. Full text, public domain.

title: A System of Logic, Ratiocinative and Inductive
creator: John Stuart Mill
description: Mill's great treatise on scientific method — a major work absent from the library. Full text, public domain.

title: The Age of Reason
creator: Thomas Paine
description: Paine's great deist manifesto — a major work absent from the library. Full text, public domain.

title: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
creator: Mary Wollstonecraft
description: The founding text of feminism — absent from the library. Full text, public domain.

title: The Adventures of Gil Blas of Santillane, Vol. 1
creator: Alain-René Lesage (Tobias Smollett, trans.)
description: Smollett's landmark 1749 translation of Lesage — the translation that naturalized the picaresque novel in English. Full text, public domain.

title: The Adventures of Gil Blas of Santillane, Vol. 2
creator: Alain-René Lesage (Tobias Smollett, trans.)
description: Vol. 2 of Smollett's Gil Blas. Full text, public domain.

title: The Adventures of Gil Blas of Santillane, Vol. 3
creator: Alain-René Lesage (Tobias Smollett, trans.)
description: Vol. 3 of Smollett's Gil Blas. Full text, public domain.

title: Wilhelm Meister's Apprenticeship and Travels, Vol. 1
creator: J. W. von Goethe (Thomas Carlyle, trans.)
description: Carlyle's landmark 1824 translation — the book that introduced German literature to Britain. Full text, public domain.

title: Wilhelm Meister's Apprenticeship and Travels, Vol. 2
creator: J. W. von Goethe (Thomas Carlyle, trans.)
description: Vol. 2 of Carlyle's Wilhelm Meister. Full text, public domain.

title: Wallenstein, Part 1: The Piccolomini
creator: Friedrich Schiller (S. T. Coleridge, trans.)
description: Coleridge's landmark 1800 translation of Schiller — a turning point in English Romantic drama. Full text, public domain.

title: Wallenstein, Part 2: The Death of Wallenstein
creator: Friedrich Schiller (S. T. Coleridge, trans.)
description: Part 2 of Coleridge's Wallenstein. Full text, public domain.

title: The Heimskringla; Or, Chronicle of the Kings of Norway
creator: Snorri Sturluson (Samuel Laing, trans.)
description: Laing's 1844 first English translation of the kings' sagas — the foundation of Norse history in English. Full text, public domain.

title: The Story of Burnt Njal
creator: George Webbe Dasent (trans.)
description: Dasent's 1861 first English translation of Njal's Saga — the greatest Icelandic saga in its landmark English dress. Full text, public domain.

title: Chronicle of the Cid
creator: Robert Southey (trans.)
description: Southey's 1808 first English Cid — the landmark English version of Spain's national epic. Full text, public domain.

title: Quo Vadis: A Narrative of the Time of Nero
creator: Henryk Sienkiewicz (Jeremiah Curtin, trans.)
description: Curtin's first English translation of the Nobel-winning novel — absent from the library. Full text, public domain.

title: Resurrection
creator: Leo Tolstoy (Louise and Aylmer Maude, trans.)
description: The Maudes' landmark authorized translation of Tolstoy's last novel. Full text, public domain.

title: Pan Tadeusz; Or, The Last Foray in Lithuania
creator: Adam Mickiewicz (George Rapall Noyes, trans.)
description: Noyes's 1917 first complete English translation of Poland's national epic. Full text, public domain.

title: Faust: A Dramatic Poem
creator: J. W. von Goethe (Abraham Hayward, trans.)
description: Hayward's 1833 first complete English Faust in prose — the translation that introduced Faust to English readers. Full text, public domain.

title: The Thousand and One Nights, Vol. 1
creator: Edward William Lane (trans.)
description: Lane's 1838-40 landmark scholarly translation of the Arabian Nights — the first complete scholarly English version. Full text, public domain.

title: The Darling and Other Stories
creator: Anton Chekhov (Constance Garnett, trans.)
description: Garnett's first-English Chekhov (1916) — the translations that introduced Chekhov to the English-speaking world. Full text, public domain.

title: The Schoolmistress and Other Stories
creator: Anton Chekhov (Constance Garnett, trans.)
description: A second volume of Garnett's landmark Chekhov translations. Full text, public domain.

title: Sextus Empiricus and Greek Scepticism
creator: Mary Mills Patrick
source: Internet Archive (sextusempiricus00patrgoog), Google Books scan of the 1899 edition
description: Mary Mills Patrick's 1899 study of Greek scepticism, containing the first English translation of Sextus Empiricus's 'Pyrrhonic Sketches' (Outlines of Pyrrhonism), Book I — the foundational text of ancient scepticism and the primary source for Pyrrhonist philosophy.

title: The Theological Tractates and The Consolation of Philosophy
creator: Boethius (H. F. Stewart and E. K. Rand, trans.)
source: Project Gutenberg ebook 13316 (transcribed from the 1918 Loeb edition)
description: The Loeb edition of Boethius: the five Theological Tractates in the Stewart/Rand translation and the Consolation of Philosophy in the 1609 'I.T.' translation as revised by Stewart. The Consolation is the most-read philosophical work of the Middle Ages; the Tractates are the foundation of medieval Trinitarian theology.

title: St. Anselm: Proslogium; Monologium; An Appendix in Behalf of the Fool by Gaunilon; and Cur Deus Homo
creator: St. Anselm of Canterbury (Sidney Norton Deane, trans.)
source: Internet Archive (bwb_C0-AJV-409), scan of the 1903 Open Court edition
description: Deane's 1903 translation of Anselm's major works: the Proslogium (containing the ontological argument for God's existence), the Monologium, Gaunilon's reply 'In Behalf of the Fool,' and Cur Deus Homo (the satisfaction theory of the atonement) — the founding texts of scholastic philosophy.

title: Historia Calamitatum: The Story of My Misfortunes
creator: Peter Abelard (Henry Adams Bellows, trans.)
description: Abelard's autobiographical 'Story of My Misfortunes' — the great 12th-century dialectician's account of his castration, condemnation, and love affair with Heloise — in Henry Adams Bellows's 1922 translation. The most famous medieval autobiography after Augustine's Confessions.

title: The Vision of God
creator: Nicholas of Cusa (Emma Gurney Salter, trans.)
source: Internet Archive (visionofgod00nich), scan of the 1928 Dent edition
description: Nicholas of Cusa's mystical-philosophical masterpiece 'De Visione Dei' (1453) in Emma Gurney Salter's 1928 translation, with an introduction by Evelyn Underhill. Cusa's doctrine of 'learned ignorance' and the coincidence of opposites bridges medieval mysticism and Renaissance philosophy.

title: The De Sacramento Altaris of William of Ockham
creator: William of Ockham (T. Bruce Birch, ed. and trans.)
source: Internet Archive (desacramentoalta0000unse), scan of the 1930 Birch edition
description: Birch's 1930 critical edition and English translation of Ockham's 'De Sacramento Altaris' — the only complete work of William of Ockham available in a public-domain English translation. Latin text with facing English translation; the key source for Ockham's nominalism and eucharistic theology.

title: Selections from Medieval Philosophers, Vol. II: Roger Bacon to William of Ockham
creator: Richard McKeon (ed. and trans.)
source: Internet Archive (selectionsfromme0002roge), scan of the 1930 Scribner's edition
description: McKeon's landmark 1930 anthology, Vol. II: Roger Bacon, Bonaventure, Aquinas, Matthew of Aquasparta, Duns Scotus, and William of Ockham — including the only public-domain English selections of Scotus (Oxford Commentary, Bk I) and Ockham (Quodlibetal Questions). The standard gateway to medieval philosophy for a generation.

title: The Philosophical Works of Descartes, Vol. I
creator: Rene Descartes (Elizabeth S. Haldane and G. R. T. Ross, trans.)
source: Internet Archive (isbn_052109416x), scan of a later reprint of the 1911 first edition
description: Vol. I of the Haldane & Ross translation — the standard English Descartes for most of the 20th century: Rules for the Direction of the Mind, Discourse on Method, Meditations on First Philosophy, Principles of Philosophy (selections), The Search after Truth, The Passions of the Soul, and Notes against a Programme.

title: The Philosophical Works of Descartes, Vol. II: Objections and Replies
creator: Rene Descartes (Elizabeth S. Haldane and G. R. T. Ross, trans.)
source: Internet Archive (philosophicalwor0002eliz_z6i5), scan of a later reprint of the 1912 first edition
description: Vol. II of Haldane & Ross: the complete Objections and Replies to the Meditations (Caterus, Hobbes, Arnauld, Gassendi, Bourdin and others, with Descartes's replies) — the essential companion to the Meditations, containing the great early-modern debates on mind, God, and knowledge.

title: The Chief Works of Benedict de Spinoza, Vol. I
creator: Benedict de Spinoza (R. H. M. Elwes, trans.)
source: Internet Archive (chiefworksbened00elwegoog), Google Books scan of the 1891 reprint of the revised edition
description: Vol. I of Elwes's Bohn translation: the Tractatus Theologico-Politicus (Spinoza's founding text of biblical criticism and political liberalism) and the unfinished Tractatus Politicus, with Elwes's introduction. The classic Victorian English Spinoza.

title: The Chief Works of Benedict de Spinoza, Vol. II
creator: Benedict de Spinoza (R. H. M. Elwes, trans.)
source: Internet Archive (chiefworksbened03elwegoog), Google Books scan of the 1891 reprint of the revised edition
description: Vol. II of Elwes's Bohn translation: 'On the Improvement of the Understanding' (De Intellectus Emendatione), the Ethics, and the Select Letters — Spinoza's complete system of metaphysics, ethics, and correspondence in the standard Victorian translation.

title: New Essays Concerning Human Understanding
creator: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (Alfred G. Langley, trans.)
source: Internet Archive (newessaysconcern00lei), scan of the 1896 Macmillan edition
description: Langley's 1896 translation of Leibniz's 'Nouveaux Essais' — the great point-by-point rationalist reply to Locke's Essay Concerning Human Understanding, and Leibniz's fullest statement of innate ideas, perception, and the nature of substance.

title: A System of Logic, Ratiocinative and Inductive, Vol. I
creator: John Stuart Mill
source: Internet Archive (systemoflogicrat01millrich), scan of the 1843 first edition, Vol. I
description: Vol. I of Mill's 'System of Logic' (first edition, 1843): Books I–III — names and propositions, reasoning, and the beginning of induction. The founding text of inductive logic and the philosophy of science; Mill's methods of induction remade scientific reasoning.

title: A System of Logic, Ratiocinative and Inductive, Vol. II
creator: John Stuart Mill
source: Internet Archive (systemoflogicrat02millrich), scan of the 1843 first edition, Vol. II
description: Vol. II of Mill's 'System of Logic' (1843): Books III (continued) through VI — induction, fallacies, and the logic of the moral sciences, including the famous defense of the social sciences as sciences. Completes the 1843 first edition.

title: Two Treatises of Government
creator: John Locke
source: Internet Archive (bim_eighteenth-century_two-treatises-of-governm_locke-john_1764); long-s normalized to s
description: Locke's 'Two Treatises of Government' — the First Treatise demolishing Filmer's divine right, the Second founding liberal political philosophy on natural rights, property, and the right of revolution. The charter text of modern constitutionalism; this printing carries Locke's final corrections.

title: A Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge
creator: George Berkeley
description: Berkeley's 'Principles of Human Knowledge' (1710): 'esse est percipi' — the definitive statement of immaterialism, arguing that matter does not exist and that reality consists of minds and their ideas. The central text of British empiricist metaphysics.

title: Epictetus: The Discourses as Reported by Arrian, the Manual, and Fragments, Vol. I
creator: Epictetus (W. A. Oldfather, trans.)
source: English Wikisource (transcribed from the 1925 Loeb edition)
description: Vol. I of Oldfather's Loeb Epictetus — the standard scholarly English translation: the Discourses (as reported by Arrian), Books I and II. The core text of Roman Stoicism, complementing the Matheson translation already in the library with the complete critical edition.

title: Epictetus: The Discourses as Reported by Arrian, the Manual, and Fragments, Vol. II
creator: Epictetus (W. A. Oldfather, trans.)
source: English Wikisource (transcribed from the 1928 Loeb edition)
description: Vol. II of Oldfather's Loeb Epictetus: Discourses Books III–IV, the Enchiridion (Manual), and the Fragments, with index. Completes the Loeb set; the Enchiridion is the most influential Stoic handbook ever written.

title: Mutual Aid: A Factor of Evolution
creator: Peter Kropotkin
description: Kropotkin's landmark argument that cooperation, not competition, drives evolution — the scientific cornerstone of anarchist communism.

title: The Conquest of Bread
creator: Peter Kropotkin
description: The classic program of anarchist communism: production for need, distribution by free agreement, and the abolition of the wage system.

title: Memoirs of a Revolutionist
creator: Peter Kropotkin
description: Kropotkin's autobiography: from Russian prince and geographer to the leading theorist of anarchism.

title: Fields, Factories and Workshops
creator: Peter Kropotkin
description: Kropotkin's vision of decentralized industry integrated with agriculture — the founding text of the anarchist economics of scale.

title: God and the State
creator: Mikhail Bakunin (Benjamin R. Tucker, trans.)
description: Bakunin's unfinished polemic against God and the State; the founding text of collectivist anarchism. Translated by Benjamin R. Tucker.

title: What is Property? An Inquiry into the Principle of Right and of Government
creator: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon (Benjamin R. Tucker, trans.)
description: The 1840 memoir that asked 'What is property?' and answered 'Property is robbery' — the founding text of anarchism. Translated by Benjamin R. Tucker.

title: General Idea of the Revolution in the Nineteenth Century
creator: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon (John Beverley Robinson, trans.)
description: Proudhon's 1851 program for the revolution: federalism, mutualism, and the dissolution of government into economic organization. Translated by John Beverley Robinson.

title: System of Economical Contradictions; or, The Philosophy of Misery
creator: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon (Benjamin R. Tucker, trans.)
description: Proudhon's 'Philosophy of Misery' — the critique of political economy that provoked Marx's 'Poverty of Philosophy'. Translated by Benjamin R. Tucker.

title: The Ego and His Own
creator: Max Stirner (Steven T. Byington, trans.)
description: The founding text of individualist anarchism and egoism: the war of the Unique against every abstraction — State, Church, and Humanity. Translated by Steven T. Byington.

title: Anarchism and Other Essays
creator: Emma Goldman
description: Goldman's essential essays on anarchism, marriage, patriotism, and the traffic in women — the American anarchist manifesto.

title: My Disillusionment in Russia
creator: Emma Goldman
description: Goldman's firsthand account of the Russian Revolution's betrayal — the anarchist break with Bolshevism.

title: Prison Memoirs of an Anarchist
creator: Alexander Berkman
description: Berkman's memoir of fourteen years in American prisons after the Homestead attentat — a classic of prison literature and anarchist autobiography.

title: The ABC of Anarchism
creator: Alexander Berkman
description: Berkman's plain-language exposition of communist anarchism — 'among the best introductions to the ideas of anarchism in the English language' (Stuart Christie). First published 1929 by Vanguard Press as 'Now and After: The ABC of Communist Anarchism'.

title: Instead of a Book, by a Man Too Busy to Write One
creator: Benjamin R. Tucker
description: Tucker's collected writings: the American individualist-anarchist program — 'State Socialism and Anarchism' and the war on the four monopolies.

title: De la division du travail social
creator: Émile Durkheim
description: Durkheim's doctoral thesis: the division of labor as the basis of social solidarity — the founding work of sociology as a science. In French; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Le Suicide: étude de sociologie
creator: Émile Durkheim
description: The founding work of quantitative sociology: suicide rates as social facts, proving the social determines the individual. In French; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Les Formes élémentaires de la vie religieuse
creator: Émile Durkheim
description: Durkheim's theory of religion from totemism: the sacred as society worshipping itself — the founding text of the sociology of religion. In French; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Les Règles de la méthode sociologique
creator: Émile Durkheim
description: The manifesto of sociological method: social facts as things, and the rules for studying them. In French; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Philosophie des Geldes
creator: Georg Simmel
description: Simmel's philosophy of money: how the money economy reshapes modern life, freedom, and individuality. In German; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Gemeinschaft und Gesellschaft
creator: Ferdinand Tönnies
description: Tönnies' distinction of Gemeinschaft (community) and Gesellschaft (society) — the founding dichotomy of sociology. First edition, 1887. In German; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Die Akkumulation des Kapitals
creator: Rosa Luxemburg
description: Luxemburg's theory of capitalist accumulation and imperialism: capital's need for non-capitalist milieus. In German; the standard English translation (1951) remains under copyright.

title: A Treatise on Man and the Development of His Faculties
creator: Adolphe Quetelet
description: The founding work of social statistics: the 'average man' and the discovery of statistical regularity in human behavior. Translated from the French, 1842.

title: Dynamic Sociology, Vol. 1
creator: Lester F. Ward
description: Ward's Dynamic Sociology, Vol. 1: the first systematic American sociology — social forces and the critique of laissez-faire.

title: Dynamic Sociology, Vol. 2
creator: Lester F. Ward
description: Ward's Dynamic Sociology, Vol. 2: completes the system — applied social science and the program of social reform.

title: The Philadelphia Negro: A Social Study
creator: W. E. B. Du Bois
description: The first sociological study of an American Black community — the founding work of urban sociology in the United States.

title: An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations
creator: Adam Smith (Edwin Cannan, ed.)
description: The founding text of modern economics: the division of labor, the invisible hand, and the critique of mercantilism. Edwin Cannan's edition.

title: The Theory of Moral Sentiments
creator: Adam Smith
description: Smith's theory of sympathy and the impartial spectator — the moral philosophy behind the Wealth of Nations.

title: Essai sur la nature du commerce en général
creator: Richard Cantillon
description: The first systematic treatise on economics: value, money, and the entrepreneur. First edition, 1755. In French; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Utilitarianism
creator: John Stuart Mill
description: Mill's defense of the greatest-happiness principle — the canonical statement of utilitarian ethics.

title: A System of Logic, Ratiocinative and Inductive, Vol. 1
creator: John Stuart Mill
description: Mill's System of Logic, Vol. 1 (1843 first edition): names, propositions, and induction — the founding text of the philosophy of science.

title: A System of Logic, Ratiocinative and Inductive, Vol. 2
creator: John Stuart Mill
description: Mill's System of Logic, Vol. 2 (1843 first edition): induction continued, fallacies, and the logic of the moral sciences.

title: The Theory of Political Economy
creator: W. Stanley Jevons
description: The marginalist revolution: utility as the mathematical basis of economics. Second edition, 1879.

title: Grundsätze der Volkswirtschaftslehre
creator: Carl Menger
description: The founding text of the Austrian school: subjective value and marginal utility. In German; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Progress and Poverty
creator: Henry George
description: Henry George's single-tax argument: why poverty persists amid progress — the best-selling economics book of the 19th century.

title: The Law
creator: Frédéric Bastiat
description: Bastiat's defense of natural law against legal plunder — the classic statement of classical-liberal legal philosophy.

title: The Theory of the Leisure Class
creator: Thorstein Veblen
description: Veblen's theory of conspicuous consumption and the leisure class — the founding text of institutional economics.

title: Evolutionary Socialism
creator: Eduard Bernstein (Edith C. Harvey, trans.)
description: Bernstein's revisionist manifesto: the case for evolutionary over revolutionary socialism — the founding document of social democracy. Translated by Edith C. Harvey, 1909.

title: The Class Struggle (Erfurt Program)
creator: Karl Kautsky (William E. Bohn, trans.)
description: Kautsky's commentary on the Erfurt Program: the orthodox Marxist synthesis of the Second International. Translated by William E. Bohn, 1910.

title: The Dictatorship of the Proletariat
creator: Karl Kautsky (H. J. Stenning, trans.)
description: Kautsky's critique of Bolshevik dictatorship — the text that split Marxism over democracy. Translated by H. J. Stenning, 1919.

title: Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism
creator: Vladimir Lenin
description: Lenin's theory of imperialism as the highest stage of capitalism — finance capital, monopolies, and the partition of the world. Vanguard Press edition, 1926.

title: The State and Revolution
creator: Vladimir Lenin
description: Lenin's theory of the state: the dictatorship of the proletariat and the withering away of the state. Vanguard Press edition, 1926.

title: Imperialism and World Economy
creator: Nikolai Bukharin
description: Bukharin's companion to Lenin: finance capital and the world economy — the Marxist theory of imperialism's economics. International Publishers, 1929.

title: The Code of Hammurabi, King of Babylon
creator: Robert Francis Harper (trans.)
description: The oldest complete legal code: the laws of Babylon, c. 1754 BCE. Translated by Robert Francis Harper.

title: The Institutes of Gaius
creator: Gaius (James Muirhead, trans.)
description: Gaius' Institutes (c. 160 CE): the Roman law textbook that taught law for a millennium. Translated by James Muirhead.

title: The Institutes of Justinian
creator: Justinian I (Thomas Collett Sandars, trans.)
description: Justinian's Institutes (533 CE): Roman law codified — the foundation of civil-law systems worldwide. Translated by Thomas Collett Sandars (1st ed. 1853).

title: The Rights of War and Peace
creator: Hugo Grotius (A. C. Campbell, trans.)
description: The founding text of international law: just war, natural law, and the law of nations. Translated by A. C. Campbell.
