description: Fichte's Die Bestimmung des Menschen (1800) — his most widely read work: doubt, knowledge, and faith in dialogue form. William Smith's 1848 translation, the first English rendering.

title: Addresses to the German Nation
creator: Johann Gottlieb Fichte (R. F. Jones and G. H. Turnbull, trans.)
description: Fichte's Reden an die deutsche Nation (1808) — the addresses that made philosophy a political force in the Napoleonic age. R. F. Jones and G. H. Turnbull's 1922 translation.

title: System des transcendentalen Idealismus
creator: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling
description: Schelling's System des transcendentalen Idealismus (1800) — nature-philosophy and the identity system; the bridge from Fichte to Hegel. German first edition. No public-domain English translation exists; reproduced as a documentary text.

title: On Religion: Speeches to Its Cultured Despisers
creator: Friedrich Schleiermacher (John Oman, trans.)
description: Schleiermacher's Reden über die Religion (1799) — the founding text of modern liberal theology: religion as intuition and feeling. John Oman's 1893 translation.

title: Schleiermacher's Soliloquies
creator: Friedrich Schleiermacher (Horace Leland Friess, trans.)
description: Schleiermacher's Monologen (1800) — the romantic self in dialogue with itself. Horace Leland Friess's 1926 translation.

title: The Christian Faith
creator: Friedrich Schleiermacher (H. R. Mackintosh and J. S. Stewart, trans.)
description: Schleiermacher's Der christliche Glaube (1821–22) — the magnum opus of liberal Protestant theology: the feeling of absolute dependence. H. R. Mackintosh and J. S. Stewart's 1928 translation, complete.

title: The Philosophical Theory of the State
creator: Bernard Bosanquet
description: Bosanquet's The Philosophical Theory of the State (1899) — British idealism's definitive political philosophy: the 'general will' in English dress. 1910 second-edition text.

title: Logic, or The Morphology of Knowledge, Vol. 1
creator: Bernard Bosanquet
description: Bosanquet's Logic, or the Morphology of Knowledge (1888), Vol. 1 — the British idealist logic: judgment and inference as the mind's self-development.

title: Logic, or The Morphology of Knowledge, Vol. 2
creator: Bernard Bosanquet
description: Bosanquet's Logic, or the Morphology of Knowledge (1888), Vol. 2.

title: Knowledge and Reality: A Criticism of Mr. F. H. Bradley's 'Principles of Logic'
creator: Bernard Bosanquet
description: Bosanquet's Knowledge and Reality (1885) — a criticism of F. H. Bradley's Principles of Logic; the opening shot of the British idealist debates.

title: The Science of Education
creator: Johann Friedrich Herbart (Henry M. and Emmie Felkin, trans.)
description: Herbart's Allgemeine Pädagogik (1806) — the founding text of scientific pedagogy: education deduced from ethics and psychology. Henry M. and Emmie Felkin's translation.

title: Outlines of Educational Doctrine
creator: Johann Friedrich Herbart (Alexis F. Lange, trans.)
description: Herbart's Umriss pädagogischer Vorlesungen (1841) — the concise system of his educational doctrine. Alexis F. Lange's 1901 translation.

title: A Text-book in Psychology
creator: Johann Friedrich Herbart (Margaret K. Smith, trans.)
description: Herbart's Lehrbuch zur Psychologie (1816) — psychology as the mechanics of ideas, the root of his pedagogy. Margaret K. Smith's 1891 translation.

title: A History of Philosophy
creator: Wilhelm Windelband (James H. Tufts, trans.)
description: Windelband's Geschichte der Philosophie (1892) — the classic 'problem-history' of philosophy from the Baden school. James H. Tufts's 1893 translation (1901 printing).

title: The Meaning and Value of Life
creator: Rudolf Eucken (W. J. Gibson, trans.)
description: Eucken's Der Sinn und Wert des Lebens (1908) — the 1908 Nobel laureate's philosophy of the spiritual life. W. J. Gibson's translation.

title: The Problem of Human Life
creator: Rudolf Eucken (W. S. Hough and W. R. Boyce Gibson, trans.)
description: Eucken's Lebensanschauungen grosser Denker — the great thinkers on life's problem, from Plato to the present. W. S. Hough and W. R. Boyce Gibson's 1909 translation.

title: The Life of the Spirit: An Introduction to Philosophy
creator: Rudolf Eucken (F. L. Pogson, trans.)
description: Eucken's Einführung in eine Philosophie des Geisteslebens — his introduction to the philosophy of the spiritual life. F. L. Pogson's 1909 translation.

title: The Truth of Religion
creator: Rudolf Eucken (W. Tudor Jones, trans.)
description: Eucken's Der Wahrheitsgehalt der Religion (1901) — the philosophy of religion of the 1908 Nobel laureate. W. Tudor Jones's translation (1913 second-edition text).

title: Main Currents of Modern Thought
creator: Rudolf Eucken (Meyrick Booth, trans.)
description: Eucken's Geistige Strömungen der Gegenwart (1904) — main currents of modern thought: the spiritual and intellectual movements of the age. Meyrick Booth's 1912 translation.

title: The Contingency of the Laws of Nature
creator: Émile Boutroux (Fred Rothwell, trans.)
description: Boutroux's De la contingence des lois de la nature (1874) — the thesis that natural laws are contingent: a founding text of French spiritualism. Fred Rothwell's 1916 translation.

title: Natural Law in Science and Philosophy
creator: Émile Boutroux (Fred Rothwell, trans.)
description: Boutroux's De l'idée de loi naturelle (1895) — natural law in science and philosophy. Rothwell's 1914 translation.

title: William James
creator: Émile Boutroux (Archibald and Barbara Henderson, trans.)
description: Boutroux's William James (1911) — the French spiritualist on the American pragmatist. Archibald and Barbara Henderson's 1912 translation.

title: Historical Studies in Philosophy
creator: Émile Boutroux (Fred Rothwell, trans.)
description: Boutroux's Études d'histoire de la philosophie — historical studies in philosophy. Rothwell's 1912 translation.

title: Logic, Vol. 1
creator: Christoph Sigwart (Helen Dendy, trans.)
description: Sigwart's Logik (1873–78), Vol. 1 — the great German logic of judgment: the logic that shaped Frege's context. Helen Dendy's 1895 translation.

title: Logic, Vol. 2
creator: Christoph Sigwart (Helen Dendy, trans.)
description: Sigwart's Logik, Vol. 2 — method and the logic of the sciences. Dendy's 1895 translation.

title: Riddles of the Sphinx: A Study in the Philosophy of Evolution
creator: F. C. S. Schiller
description: F. C. S. Schiller's Riddles of the Sphinx (1891) — the founding manifesto of humanist pragmatism, first issued as by 'A. Troglodyte'.

title: Humanism: Philosophical Essays
creator: F. C. S. Schiller
description: F. C. S. Schiller's Humanism (1903) — philosophical essays of the Oxford pragmatist: the humanist program.

title: Studies in Humanism
creator: F. C. S. Schiller
description: F. C. S. Schiller's Studies in Humanism (1907) — second series of humanist essays.

title: Formal Logic: A Scientific and Social Problem
creator: F. C. S. Schiller
description: F. C. S. Schiller's Formal Logic (1912) — the pragmatist attack on formal logic: logic as a human instrument.

title: Philosophical Discussions
creator: Chauncey Wright (Charles Eliot Norton, ed.)
description: Chauncey Wright's Philosophical Discussions (1877) — the essays of Darwin's American bulldog and Peirce's mentor, edited by Charles Eliot Norton.

title: The Science of Ethics
creator: Leslie Stephen
description: Leslie Stephen's The Science of Ethics (1882) — evolutionary ethics from the great agnostic man of letters.

title: An Agnostic's Apology, and Other Essays
creator: Leslie Stephen
description: Leslie Stephen's An Agnostic's Apology (1876) and other essays — the classic Victorian statement of agnosticism.

title: Naturalism and Agnosticism, Vol. 1
creator: James Ward
description: James Ward's Naturalism and Agnosticism (1899), Vol. 1 — the Gifford Lectures: the Cambridge pluralist's critique of naturalism.

title: Naturalism and Agnosticism, Vol. 2
creator: James Ward
description: James Ward's Naturalism and Agnosticism (1899), Vol. 2.

title: The Realm of Ends; or, Pluralism and Theism
creator: James Ward
description: James Ward's The Realm of Ends (1911) — the Gifford Lectures on pluralism and theism.

title: Psychological Principles
creator: James Ward
description: James Ward's Psychological Principles (1918) — the Cambridge psychologist-philosopher's system: the authoritative British psychology of its day.

title: A Sketch of Morality Independent of Obligation or Sanction
creator: Jean-Marie Guyau (Gertrude Kapteyn, trans.)
description: Jean-Marie Guyau's Esquisse d'une morale sans obligation ni sanction (1884) — morality without obligation or sanction: the French ethics of life. Gertrude Kapteyn's 1898 translation.

title: Esquisse d'une classification systématique des doctrines philosophiques, Vol. 1
creator: Charles Renouvier
description: Charles Renouvier's Esquisse d'une classification systématique des doctrines philosophiques (1885), Vol. 1 — French neocriticism's systematic map of philosophies. French original (BnF/Gallica scan); no PD English exists.

title: Esquisse d'une classification systématique des doctrines philosophiques, Vol. 2
creator: Charles Renouvier
description: Renouvier's Esquisse d'une classification systématique des doctrines philosophiques (1886), Vol. 2. French original.

title: Einleitung in die Geisteswissenschaften
creator: Wilhelm Dilthey
description: Wilhelm Dilthey's Einleitung in die Geisteswissenschaften (1883) — the founding charter of the human sciences: Naturwissenschaften vs. Geisteswissenschaften. German first edition; standard English translations are post-1930.

title: System der Philosophie als evidente Wissenschaft
creator: Jakob Friedrich Fries
description: Jakob Friedrich Fries's System der Philosophie als evidente Wissenschaft (1804) — the Kant-Friesian system; founder of the Friesian school. German original.

title: L'évolutionnisme des idées-forces
creator: Alfred Fouillée
description: Alfred Fouillée's L'évolutionnisme des idées-forces (1890) — the doctrine of idea-forces: ideas as forces in evolution. French original. (His Psychologie des idées-forces vol. 2 was not locatable; this single-volume work states the doctrine completely.)

title: The Logic of Hegel
creator: G. W. F. Hegel (William Wallace, trans.)
description: Hegel's Encyclopaedia Logic (1817) — the 'lesser Logic': being, essence, and notion in the system's first part. William Wallace's 1874 translation, the classic English Hegel.

title: Hegel's Philosophy of Mind
creator: G. W. F. Hegel (William Wallace, trans.)
description: Hegel's Philosophy of Mind (1830; Encyclopaedia Part 3) — subjective, objective, and absolute spirit. Wallace's 1894 translation.

title: On the Fourfold Root of the Principle of Sufficient Reason
creator: Arthur Schopenhauer (Mme. Karl Hillebrand, trans.)
description: Schopenhauer's Über die vierfache Wurzel des Satzes vom zureichenden Grunde (1813) — his doctoral dissertation: the epistemological root of the whole system. Mme. Karl Hillebrand's 1891 translation.

title: The Basis of Morality
creator: Arthur Schopenhauer (A. Bullock, trans.)
description: Schopenhauer's Preisschrift über die Grundlage der Moral (1840) — his prize essay on the basis of morals: compassion as the root of ethics. A. Bullock's 1903 translation.

title: The Catechism of Positive Religion
creator: Auguste Comte (Richard Congreve, trans.)
description: Comte's Catéchisme positiviste (1852) — positivism as the Religion of Humanity, in catechism form. Richard Congreve's 1858 translation.

title: Grundsätze der Philosophie der Zukunft
creator: Ludwig Feuerbach
description: Feuerbach's Grundsätze der Philosophie der Zukunft (1843) — the theses that turned Marx from Hegel to materialism. German original; no PD English translation exists.

title: The Theory of Heat Radiation
creator: Max Planck (Morton Masius, trans.)
description: Max Planck (1858-1947), Masius 1914 — the authorized English translation of Vorlesungen über die Theorie der Wärmestrahlung: the founding text of quantum theory, where the quantum of action h first enters physics. The pivotal birth certificate of the quantum.

title: On the Constitution of Atoms and Molecules (Parts I-III)
creator: Niels Bohr
description: Niels Bohr (1885-1962), Philosophical Magazine 1913 — the complete trilogy (Parts I-III): the Bohr model of the atom, quantized electron orbits, the explanation of the hydrogen spectrum and the periodic table's structure. The paper that made quantum theory do chemistry.

title: Electricity and Matter
creator: J. J. Thomson
description: J. J. Thomson (1856-1940) — the 1903 Silliman Lectures at Yale: the discoverer of the electron expounds the corpuscular theory, cathode rays, and the electrical structure of matter. The electron's discoverer makes the case.

title: The Corpuscular Theory of Matter
creator: J. J. Thomson
description: J. J. Thomson (1856-1940) — the full corpuscular theory: positive rays, the number of corpuscles in the atom, and the electrical origin of mass. The sequel that pushed the electron theory to its limits.

title: The Electron: Its Isolation and Measurement and the Determination of Some of Its Properties
creator: Robert A. Millikan
description: Robert A. Millikan (1868-1953) — the oil-drop experiment and the photoelectric verification of Einstein's equation: the measured charge of the electron and the experimental proof of the light quantum. The measurement that fixed e.

title: The Scientific Papers of J. Willard Gibbs, Vol. 1: Thermodynamics
creator: J. Willard Gibbs
description: J. Willard Gibbs (1839-1903), Vol. 1 of 2 — the thermodynamics papers including 'On the Equilibrium of Heterogeneous Substances': the phase rule, chemical potential, and the geometric thermodynamics that founded physical chemistry. Vol. 1 of the complete 2-vol set.

title: The Scientific Papers of J. Willard Gibbs, Vol. 2: Dynamics, Vector Analysis, Electromagnetic Theory of Light
creator: J. Willard Gibbs
description: J. Willard Gibbs (1839-1903), Vol. 2 of 2 — dynamics, vector analysis and multiple algebra (the notation physics still uses), the electromagnetic theory of light, and unpublished fragments. Vol. 2 of the complete 2-vol set.

title: Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics
creator: J. Willard Gibbs
description: J. Willard Gibbs (1839-1903) — the founding text of statistical mechanics: ensembles, the canonical distribution, and the statistical meaning of entropy. The book that gave physics its statistical soul.

title: Mécanique Céleste, Vol. 1 (Books 1-2)
creator: Pierre-Simon Laplace (Nathaniel Bowditch, trans.)
description: Pierre-Simon Laplace (1749-1827), Bowditch 1829 — Vol. 1 (Books 1-2: equilibrium, motion, universal gravitation) of the English translation with Bowditch's celebrated commentary. The 'Newton of France' in the translation that taught America celestial mechanics. Vol. 1 of 4.

title: Mécanique Céleste, Vol. 2 (Books 3-5)
creator: Pierre-Simon Laplace (Nathaniel Bowditch, trans.)
description: Pierre-Simon Laplace (1749-1827), Bowditch 1832 — Vol. 2 (Books 3-5: figures of heavenly bodies, tides, rotation) with Bowditch's commentary. Vol. 2 of 4.

title: Mécanique Céleste, Vol. 3 (Books 6-7)
creator: Pierre-Simon Laplace (Nathaniel Bowditch, trans.)
description: Pierre-Simon Laplace (1749-1827), Bowditch 1834 — Vol. 3 (Books 6-7: planetary motions, lunar theory) with Bowditch's commentary and tables. Vol. 3 of 4.

title: Mécanique Céleste, Vol. 4 (Books 8-10)
creator: Pierre-Simon Laplace (Nathaniel Bowditch, trans.)
description: Pierre-Simon Laplace (1749-1827), Bowditch 1839 — Vol. 4 (Books 8-10: satellites, comets, system of the world, capillary attraction) with Bowditch's commentary. Vol. 4 of 4, completing the set.

title: Baltimore Lectures on Molecular Dynamics and the Wave Theory of Light
creator: William Thomson, Lord Kelvin
description: Lord Kelvin (1824-1907) — the twenty 1884 Johns Hopkins lectures with twelve appendices: molecular dynamics, the wave theory of light, and the mechanical models of the ether. Kelvin thinking aloud at full power.

title: Treatise on Natural Philosophy, Part 1
creator: William Thomson (Lord Kelvin) and Peter Guthrie Tait
description: Kelvin and Tait — the Treatise (Part 1, the complete work as published): kinematics, dynamics, and the energetics that carried Newtonian mechanics into the age of energy. The 'Thomson and Tait' every physicist learned from.

title: The Principle of Relativity: A Collection of Original Memoirs
creator: H. A. Lorentz, A. Einstein, H. Minkowski, H. Weyl (W. Perrett and G. B. Jeffery, trans.)
description: The 1923 Methuen collection (Perrett/Jeffery translation) — Lorentz, Einstein, Minkowski ('Space and Time'), and Weyl's 'Gravitation and Electricity' with Sommerfeld's notes: the primary papers of special and general relativity in one volume. The relativity canon in English.

title: Relativity: The Special and General Theory
creator: Albert Einstein (Robert W. Lawson, trans.)
description: Albert Einstein (1879-1955), Lawson 1920 — Einstein's own popular exposition of special and general relativity: the book that carried relativity to the world. The master's own account.

title: The Principles of Chemistry, Vol. 1
creator: Dmitri Mendeleev (George Kamensky, trans.)
description: Dmitri Mendeleev (1834-1907), Kamensky 1897 — Vol. 1 of the English translation (6th Russian ed.): the periodic law expounded by its discoverer, from the elements in order. The periodic table from the hand that built it. Vol. 1 of 2.

title: The Principles of Chemistry, Vol. 2
creator: Dmitri Mendeleev (George Kamensky, trans.)
description: Dmitri Mendeleev (1834-1907), Kamensky 1897 — Vol. 2 of the English translation: the systematic chemistry of the elements under the periodic law. Vol. 2 of 2, completing the set.

title: Studies in Chemical Dynamics
creator: Jacobus Henricus van't Hoff (Thomas Ewan, trans.)
description: J. H. van't Hoff (1852-1911), Ewan 1896 (revised by Ernst Cohen) — chemical kinetics and the dynamics of reaction: the book that made reaction rates a science. Physical chemistry's founding kinetic text.

title: Theoretical Chemistry from the Standpoint of Avogadro's Rule and Thermodynamics
creator: Walther Nernst (L. M. Palmer, trans.)
description: Walther Nernst (1864-1941), Palmer 1904 (2nd English ed., from the 4th German ed.) — the systematization of physical chemistry: thermodynamics applied to solutions, electrochemistry, and the road to the third law. The field's great textbook.

title: Outlines of General Chemistry
creator: Wilhelm Ostwald (James Walker, trans.)
description: Wilhelm Ostwald (1853-1932), Walker 1895 (2nd ed.) — the systematizer of physical chemistry: stoichiometry, chemical dynamics, electrochemistry, and catalysis in the translation made with the author's sanction. The discipline's charter text.

title: Sketch of a Course of Chemical Philosophy
creator: Stanislao Cannizzaro
description: Stanislao Cannizzaro (1826-1910), Alembic Club Reprint No. 18 (1911) — the 1858 Sunto that revived Avogadro's hypothesis and settled atomic weights at Karlsruhe 1860: the letter that ended chemistry's atomic-weight chaos. In English translation.

title: Microscopical Researches into the Accordance in the Structure and Growth of Animals and Plants
creator: Theodor Schwann (Henry Smith, trans.)
description: Theodor Schwann (1810-1882), Smith 1847 (Sydenham Society) — the cell theory: all living things composed of cells. The founding document of cell biology, in the classic English translation.

title: Cellular Pathology as Based upon Physiological and Pathological Histology
creator: Rudolf Virchow (Frank Chance, trans.)
description: Rudolf Virchow (1821-1902), Chance 1860 — the twenty 1858 Berlin lectures: 'omnis cellula e cellula,' disease as cellular disorder. The founding text of cellular pathology.

title: The Modern Theory of Solution: Memoirs by Pfeffer, van't Hoff, Arrhenius, and Raoult
creator: Harry C. Jones (trans. and ed.)
description: Harper's Scientific Memoirs (Jones, trans./ed., 1899) — the founding papers of physical chemistry in English: Pfeffer's osmotic investigations, van't Hoff on osmotic pressure, Arrhenius 'On the Dissociation of Substances Dissolved in Water,' and Raoult's laws. The ionic-dissociation paper in PD English at last.

title: Essays on the Theory of Numbers: I. Continuity and Irrational Numbers; II. The Nature and Meaning of Numbers
creator: Richard Dedekind (Wooster Woodruff Beman, trans.)
description: Richard Dedekind (1831-1916), Beman 1901 — the Dedekind cut (continuity and irrational numbers) and the set-theoretic foundation of the natural numbers. The rigorous foundation of the real numbers.

title: The Mathematical Analysis of Logic
creator: George Boole
description: George Boole (1815-1864) — the pamphlet that founded symbolic logic: the calculus of deductive reasoning. The birth of Boolean algebra.

title: An Investigation of the Laws of Thought
creator: George Boole
description: George Boole (1815-1864) — the Laws of Thought: the mathematical theories of logic and probabilities. The book that made logic a mathematics.

title: Contributions to the Founding of the Theory of Transfinite Numbers
creator: Georg Cantor (Philip E. B. Jourdain, trans.)
description: Georg Cantor (1845-1918), Jourdain 1915 — the founding papers of set theory and transfinite numbers, with Jourdain's introduction and notes. The mathematics of infinity.

title: The Foundations of Geometry
creator: David Hilbert (E. J. Townsend, trans.)
description: David Hilbert (1862-1943), Townsend 1902 (2nd ed.) — the axiomatic foundations of geometry: the book that made rigor the standard. The axiomatic method's manifesto.

title: Geometrical Researches on the Theory of Parallels
creator: Nicholas Lobachevsky (George Bruce Halsted, trans.)
description: Nicholas Lobachevsky (1792-1856), Halsted 1891 — the founding text of non-Euclidean geometry (translation of the 1840 Geometrische Untersuchungen). The parallel postulate falls.

title: The Science Absolute of Space
creator: John Bolyai (George Bruce Halsted, trans.)
description: John Bolyai (1802-1860), Halsted 1896 (4th ed.) — the Appendix to the Tentamen (1832): absolute geometry independent of Euclid's parallel axiom, with Halsted's appendices. Non-Euclidean geometry's other founder.

title: The Geometry of René Descartes
creator: René Descartes (David Eugene Smith and Marcia L. Latham, trans.)
description: René Descartes (1596-1650), Smith/Latham 1925 (Open Court) — the Geometry (1637): analytic geometry, with facsimile of the first edition. The book that married algebra to geometry.

title: Principia Mathematica, Vol. 1 (Second Edition)
creator: Alfred North Whitehead and Bertrand Russell
description: Whitehead and Russell, Vol. 1, 2nd ed. (1925) — the logicist foundation of mathematics: *1-*43, with Russell's new introduction. The 1910 first edition was not available in a usable scan; this is the PD 1925 second edition. Vol. 1 of 3.

title: Principia Mathematica, Vol. 2
creator: Alfred North Whitehead and Bertrand Russell
description: Whitehead and Russell, Vol. 2 (1912) — cardinal and ordinal arithmetic, the theory of series. Vol. 2 of 3.

title: Principia Mathematica, Vol. 3
creator: Alfred North Whitehead and Bertrand Russell
description: Whitehead and Russell, Vol. 3 (1913) — relations, measurement, and the completion of the logicist program. Vol. 3 of 3, completing the set.

title: The Algebra of Mohammed ben Musa
creator: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi (Frederic Rosen, trans.)
description: al-Khwarizmi (c. 780-c. 850), Rosen 1831 (Oriental Translation Fund) — the founding text of algebra, in English with the Arabic. The book that gave algebra its name.

title: The Geometrical Lectures of Isaac Barrow
creator: Isaac Barrow (J. M. Child, trans.)
description: Isaac Barrow (1630-1677), Child 1916 (Open Court) — the Lectiones geometricae: Newton's teacher on the fundamental theorem of calculus, in English. The calculus before Newton.

title: An Inquiry into the Causes and Effects of the Variolae Vaccinae
creator: Edward Jenner
description: The paper that founded immunology: Jenner's 1798 announcement of vaccination against smallpox, with his case histories. The single most consequential medical publication of the era. Project Gutenberg edition.

title: Further Observations on the Variolae Vaccinae, or Cow Pox
creator: Edward Jenner
description: Jenner's 1799 sequel to the Inquiry: additional cases and replies to early critics of vaccination. 1799 London edition.

title: A Continuation of Facts and Observations Relative to the Variolae Vaccinae, or Cow Pox
creator: Edward Jenner
description: Jenner's 1800 third vaccination tract, consolidating the evidence that cowpox protects against smallpox. 1800 London edition.

title: The Origin of the Vaccine Inoculation
creator: Edward Jenner
description: Jenner's 1801 pamphlet distinguishing casual cowpox from the disease excited by inoculation — his concise history of the vaccine's origin. 1801 London edition.

title: The Principles and Practice of Medicine
creator: William Osler
description: The textbook that defined modern clinical medicine: Osler's 1892 first edition, the work that made bedside teaching and systematic clinical description the standard of medical education. Complete 1892 first edition (xvi + 1079 pp., with index); publisher's advertisements removed.

title: Aequanimitas, with Other Addresses to Medical Students, Nurses and Practitioners of Medicine
creator: William Osler
description: Osler's collected addresses — including the title essay 'Aequanimitas' — the most quoted medical humanism in English. 1904 first edition.

title: Science and Immortality
creator: William Osler
description: Osler's 1904 Ingersoll Lecture on science and immortality — his most famous philosophical address. 1904 first edition.

title: An Alabama Student, and Other Biographical Essays
creator: William Osler
description: Osler's 1908 biographical essays on physicians and scientists — the 'Alabama Student' and kindred pieces that made him medicine's chief memorialist. 1908 first edition.

title: The Evolution of Modern Medicine
creator: William Osler
description: Osler's 1913 Yale lectures on the history of medicine, published 1921 — the founding narrative of modern medical historiography. Project Gutenberg edition.

title: Notes on Nursing: What It Is, and What It Is Not
creator: Florence Nightingale
description: The founding text of modern nursing: Nightingale's 1860 manual on sanitation, observation, and care of the sick — also the founding document of medical statistics in practice. Project Gutenberg edition.

title: Subsidiary Notes as to the Introduction of Female Nursing into Military Hospitals in Peace and War
creator: Florence Nightingale
description: Nightingale's 1858 privately printed memorandum on army nursing reform — the policy paper behind the Nightingale Fund and modern military nursing. Project Gutenberg edition.

title: Notes on Hospitals
creator: Florence Nightingale
description: Nightingale's 1859 hospital-design treatise: the two Liverpool papers on ward construction plus her Royal Commission evidence and Builder articles — the founding text of evidence-based hospital architecture. 1859 first edition; publisher's catalogue removed.

title: Introductory Notes on Lying-in Institutions
creator: Florence Nightingale
description: Nightingale's 1871 study of maternity hospitals and midwifery training — pioneering hospital mortality statistics applied to childbirth. Project Gutenberg edition; publisher's catalogue removed.

title: A Treatise on the Diseases of the Chest and on Mediate Auscultation
creator: René Laennec, trans. John Forbes
description: The stethoscope's founding text in English: Sir John Forbes's 1821 translation of Laennec's 'De l'auscultation médiate' (1819), which introduced mediate auscultation and modern chest diagnosis to the English-speaking world. 1834 edition of the Forbes translation.

title: De l'auscultation médiate, ou Traité du diagnostic des maladies des poumons et du coeur, Tome I
creator: René Laennec
description: Laennec's 1819 French first edition, vol. I — the original text that invented the stethoscope and scientific chest examination. French documentary edition (no PD English of the original; the Forbes translation is staged separately).

title: De l'auscultation médiate, ou Traité du diagnostic des maladies des poumons et du coeur, Tome II
creator: René Laennec
description: Laennec's 1819 French first edition, vol. II — completing the original stethoscope treatise. French documentary edition.

title: The Seats and Causes of Diseases Investigated by Anatomy, Vol. I
creator: Giovanni Battista Morgagni, trans. Benjamin Alexander
description: Pathological anatomy founded: Benjamin Alexander's 1769 English translation of Morgagni's 'De sedibus' (1761) — 700 autopsies correlating symptoms with organ lesions, the birth of clinicopathological reasoning. Vol. I of III.

title: The Seats and Causes of Diseases Investigated by Anatomy, Vol. II
creator: Giovanni Battista Morgagni, trans. Benjamin Alexander
description: Alexander's 1769 translation of Morgagni's 'De sedibus', vol. II (ends 'End of Book III').

title: The Seats and Causes of Diseases Investigated by Anatomy, Vol. III
creator: Giovanni Battista Morgagni, trans. Benjamin Alexander
description: Alexander's 1769 translation of Morgagni's 'De sedibus', vol. III — completing the set, with the general index ('The End').

title: De sedibus, et causis morborum per anatomen indagatis libri quinque
creator: Giovanni Battista Morgagni
description: Morgagni's 1761 Latin first edition of 'De sedibus' — the original text of pathological anatomy, complete (ends 'Finis Tomi Secundi'). Latin documentary edition.

title: A Treatise on the Blood, Inflammation, and Gun-shot Wounds
creator: John Hunter
description: Hunter's posthumous masterpiece (1794): the physiology of blood and inflammation applied to surgery — the foundation of scientific surgery. First edition; bookseller's catalogue matter removed.

title: A Treatise on the Venereal Disease
creator: John Hunter
description: Hunter's 1786 treatise on venereal disease — the first systematic clinical and experimental study of syphilis and gonorrhoea, including his famous (and self-disastrous) self-inoculation experiment. First edition.

title: The Natural History of the Human Teeth
creator: John Hunter
description: Hunter's 1771 dental classic: the first scientific account of tooth structure, formation, and disease — the founding text of scientific dentistry. First edition.

title: Observations on Certain Parts of the Animal Oeconomy
creator: John Hunter
description: Hunter's 1786 comparative-anatomy papers — digestion, the lymphatics, the torpedo's electric organs — the research program that made him the father of scientific surgery. First edition.

title: Ornithological Biography, Vol. I
creator: John James Audubon
description: The text companion to 'The Birds of America': Audubon's species accounts, field observations, and American frontier narratives, vol. I (1831).

title: Ornithological Biography, Vol. II
creator: John James Audubon
description: Audubon's 'Ornithological Biography', vol. II (1834).

title: Ornithological Biography, Vol. III
creator: John James Audubon
description: Audubon's 'Ornithological Biography', vol. III (1835).

title: Ornithological Biography, Vol. IV
creator: John James Audubon
description: Audubon's 'Ornithological Biography', vol. IV (1838).

title: Ornithological Biography, Vol. V
creator: John James Audubon
description: Audubon's 'Ornithological Biography', vol. V (1839) — completing the five-volume text of 'The Birds of America'.

title: Audubon and His Journals, Vol. I
creator: John James Audubon, ed. Maria R. Audubon
description: Audubon's journals 1820–1843 (Missouri, Labrador, Florida expeditions), edited by his granddaughter Maria R. Audubon with Elliott Coues's notes — the primary record of his fieldwork. Vol. I of II, 1897 edition.

title: Audubon and His Journals, Vol. II
creator: John James Audubon, ed. Maria R. Audubon
description: Audubon's journals, vol. II (1897) — completing the set.

title: On the Mode of Communication of Cholera
creator: John Snow
description: The founding text of epidemiology: Snow's 1855 second edition with the Broad Street pump map evidence, proving cholera spreads through contaminated water. Project Gutenberg edition; publisher's catalogue removed, footnotes retained.

title: On the Inhalation of the Vapour of Ether in Surgical Operations
creator: John Snow
description: Snow's 1847 pamphlet on ether anesthesia — the first scientific dosing study of a general anesthetic, with his inhaler design and case series. 1847 first edition.

title: Zwei offene Briefe an Hofrath Dr. Eduard Casp. Jac. v. Siebold und an Hofrath Dr. F. W. Scanzoni
creator: Ignaz Semmelweis
description: Semmelweis's 1861 open letters to Siebold and Scanzoni — the primary documentary record of his fight for hand-disinfection against childbed fever. German documentary edition: no public-domain English translation exists (Carter 1983 is under copyright).

title: A Treatise on the Small-pox and Measles
creator: Rhazes (al-Razi), trans. William Alexander Greenhill
description: The first clinical distinction of smallpox from measles, by the Persian physician Rhazes (c. 910) — in William Alexander Greenhill's 1848 Sydenham Society English translation. Public domain; society member-lists removed.

title: The Poverty of Philosophy
creator: Karl Marx (Harry Quelch, trans.)
description: Marx's 1847 demolition of Proudhon's Philosophy of Poverty — the founding polemic of Marxist political economy, countering utopian moralism with historical materialism. Harry Quelch's translation (Charles H. Kerr, Chicago, 1913).

title: Wage-Labour and Capital
creator: Karl Marx (J. L. Joynes, trans.)
description: Marx's December 1847 Brussels lectures on wages, capital and exploitation — the seed-crystal of Capital, Vol. I — in the first English translation, by J. L. Joynes (Modern Press, London, 1886).

title: Value, Price and Profit
creator: Karl Marx (Eleanor Marx Aveling, ed.)
description: Marx's 1865 address to the General Council of the International — his clearest popular exposition of surplus value, wages and profit, and the limits of trade-union struggle under capitalism. First English edition, edited by Eleanor Marx Aveling (1899).

title: The Civil War in France
creator: Karl Marx
description: Marx's 1871 address on the Paris Commune — written in English for the General Council of the International — the founding Marxist analysis of the Commune as the first dictatorship of the proletariat.

title: Theses on Feuerbach
creator: Karl Marx (Austin Lewis, trans.)
description: Marx's eleven theses jotted in Brussels in spring 1845 — 'philosophers have only interpreted the world; the point is to change it' — in Austin Lewis's translation, as printed in the 1903 Kerr edition of Engels's Ludwig Feuerbach.

title: Ludwig Feuerbach and the End of Classical German Philosophy
creator: Friedrich Engels (Austin Lewis, trans.)
description: Engels's 1886 reckoning with Hegel and Feuerbach — the classic statement of dialectical vs. mechanical materialism — in Austin Lewis's translation (Charles H. Kerr, 1903). Marx's Theses on Feuerbach, printed as the edition's appendix, is staged as a separate entry.

title: Anti-Dühring: Herr Eugen Dühring's Revolution in Science
creator: Friedrich Engels (Austin Lewis, trans.)
description: Engels's full-dress 1878 defence of Marxism against Dühring — the encyclopedia of dialectical materialism (philosophy, political economy, socialism) — in Austin Lewis's translation (Charles H. Kerr, 1907).

title: The Peasant War in Germany
creator: Friedrich Engels (Moissaye J. Olgin, trans.)
description: Engels's 1850 history of the 1525 German peasant revolt — the first Marxist history, reading Münzer's rebellion through class struggle — in Moissaye J. Olgin's translation (International Publishers, 1926).

title: The Great French Revolution, 1789–1793
creator: Peter Kropotkin (N. F. Dryhurst, trans.)
description: Kropotkin's anarchist history of 1789–1793 — the Revolution told from below, through the sections, communes and peasant risings — in N. F. Dryhurst's translation (Heinemann, 1909), complete in all 68 chapters.

title: Modern Science and Anarchism
creator: Peter Kropotkin (David A. Modell, trans.)
description: Kropotkin's 1903 philosophical testament — anarchism grounded in the inductive-deductive method of modern natural science — in David A. Modell's translation (Social Science Club of Philadelphia).

title: The Quintessence of Capitalism
creator: Werner Sombart (M. Epstein, trans.)
description: Sombart's psychology of the modern businessman — the 'capitalist spirit' as a historical formation — in M. Epstein's translation (Dutton, 1915); the summit of the German historical school in English.

title: The Social Significance of the Modern Drama
creator: Emma Goldman
description: Goldman's 1914 lectures on Ibsen, Shaw, Strindberg and the modern drama as a vehicle of anarchist ideas — art criticism as social theory.

title: My Further Disillusionment in Russia
creator: Emma Goldman
description: Goldman's 1924 sequel on the Russian Revolution's betrayal — the anarchist case against Bolshevism, from Kronstadt to the crushing of the soviets.

title: Imperialism: A Study (First Edition)
creator: John A. Hobson
description: Hobson's 1902 first-edition text — the underconsumptionist theory of imperialism as the export of surplus capital — the book that shaped Lenin's and Keynes's thinking on empire. A later impression is also held as hobson-imperialism-1902.

title: The Evolution of Modern Capitalism
creator: John A. Hobson
description: Hobson's 1894 study of machine production and the displacement of labour — the founding text of underconsumptionist economics.

title: The Industrial System
creator: John A. Hobson
description: Hobson's 1909 inquiry into earned vs. unearned income — rent, monopoly and the ethics of distribution.

title: Work and Wealth: A Human Valuation
creator: John A. Hobson
description: Hobson's 1914 'human valuation' — welfare economics from the underconsumptionist side, valuing wealth by human well-being.

title: Sozialreform oder Revolution?
creator: Rosa Luxemburg
description: Luxemburg's 1899 polemic against Bernstein — the founding text of revolutionary Marxism's case that social reform cannot supersede revolution. German original; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: The Crisis in the German Social-Democracy (The Junius Pamphlet)
creator: Rosa Luxemburg
description: Luxemburg's 1916 Junius pamphlet — written in prison, the Marxist indictment of the Social Democrats' war credits — in the 1919 Socialist Publication Society English translation.

title: What Is to Be Done?
creator: Vladimir Lenin
description: Lenin's 1902 founding text of Bolshevism — the vanguard party, 'freedom of criticism' vs. dogmatism — in the 1929 International Publishers (Little Lenin Library) translation.

title: Materialism and Empirio-Criticism
creator: Vladimir Lenin (David Kvitko, trans.)
description: Lenin's 1909 philosophical defence of materialism against Machist revisionism — the epistemological foundation of dialectical materialism — in David Kvitko's 1927 translation.

title: The Instinct of Workmanship
creator: Thorstein Veblen
description: Veblen's 1914 anthropology of industry — the instinct of workmanship vs. the predatory instinct — institutional economics' deepest foundation.

title: Imperial Germany and the Industrial Revolution
creator: Thorstein Veblen
description: Veblen's 1915 study of Germany's industrial revolution — dynastic state meets machine industry — institutionalism applied to national development.

title: The Higher Learning in America
creator: Thorstein Veblen
description: Veblen's 1918 assault on the American university — business principles vs. the higher learning — the classic institutionalist critique of education.

title: The Engineers and the Price System
creator: Thorstein Veblen
description: Veblen's 1921 engineers' manifesto — the technicians vs. the price system — institutionalism's most radical programmatic statement.

title: Liberalism
creator: L. T. Hobhouse
description: Hobhouse's 1911 systematization of new liberalism — the classic statement of social liberalism's case for state action.

title: Morals in Evolution, Part I
creator: L. T. Hobhouse
description: Hobhouse's 1906 comparative ethics, Part I — the evolution of moral ideas from primitive to civilized society. Volume 1 of 2.

title: Morals in Evolution, Part II
creator: L. T. Hobhouse
description: Hobhouse's 1906 comparative ethics, Part II — the higher morality and the modern state. Volume 2 of 2, completing the work.

title: Human Nature in Politics
creator: Graham Wallas
description: Wallas's 1908 founding text of political psychology — impulse, habit and non-rational politics against intellectualist models — in the 1920 third edition text.

title: The Great Society
creator: Graham Wallas
description: Wallas's 1914 psychological analysis of the Great Society — the maladaptation of human nature to industrial civilization.

title: Cours d'économie politique, Tome I
creator: Vilfredo Pareto
description: Pareto's 1896-97 Lausanne lectures — the founding text of the Lausanne school, general equilibrium and the first statement of Pareto optimality. French original; no public-domain English translation exists. Volume 1 of 2.

title: Cours d'économie politique, Tome II
creator: Vilfredo Pareto
description: Pareto's Lausanne lectures, volume 2 — completing the Cours. French original; no public-domain English translation exists. Volume 2 of 2.

title: Trattato di sociologia generale, Volume I
creator: Vilfredo Pareto
description: Pareto's 1916 masterwork of sociology — residues and derivations, the circulation of elites. Italian original; no public-domain English translation exists. Volume 1 of 2.

title: Trattato di sociologia generale, Volume II
creator: Vilfredo Pareto
description: Pareto's sociology masterwork, volume 2 — completing the Trattato. Italian original; no public-domain English translation exists. Volume 2 of 2.

title: Manuale di economia politica
creator: Vilfredo Pareto
description: Pareto's 1919 manual — the compact statement of his economics: ophelimity, indifference curves, the Pareto optimum. Italian original; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Les Systèmes socialistes, Tome I
creator: Vilfredo Pareto
description: Pareto's 1902 survey of socialist systems — the Lausanne lectures on socialism, from utopians to Marx. French original; no public-domain English translation exists. Volume 1 of 2.

title: Les Systèmes socialistes, Tome II
creator: Vilfredo Pareto
description: Pareto's survey of socialist systems, volume 2 — completing Les Systèmes socialistes. French original; no public-domain English translation exists. Volume 2 of 2.

title: The Jews and Modern Capitalism
creator: Werner Sombart (M. Epstein, trans.)
description: Sombart's 1911 study of Jewish economic history and the spirit of capitalism — the great counterpart to Weber's Protestant Ethic. In M. Epstein's 1913 English translation. Preserved as economic history; its theses on Jewish economic life are contested and presented here as a document of early-20th-century social thought, not as endorsement.

title: Lectures on Justice, Police, Revenue and Arms
creator: Adam Smith (Edwin Cannan, ed.)
description: Smith's 1762-63 Glasgow lectures on jurisprudence — justice, police, revenue and arms — the lost foundation of the Wealth of Nations, recovered from student notes.

title: Essays on Philosophical Subjects
creator: Adam Smith
description: Smith's posthumous 1795 essays — the History of Astronomy, the Theory of the External Senses — the philosopher behind the economist.

title: The High Price of Bullion
creator: David Ricardo
description: Ricardo's 1810 bullion pamphlet — the quantity theory applied to the Bank Restriction, the tract that made his name.

title: Essay on the Influence of a Low Price of Corn on the Profits of Stock
creator: David Ricardo
description: Ricardo's 1815 Essay on Profits — the corn model that became the core of the Principles — extracted from McCulloch's 1846 Works.

title: Principles of Political Economy
creator: T. R. Malthus
description: Malthus's 1820 Principles — the great anti-Ricardian treatise: effective demand, gluts, and the limits of Say's Law.

title: Reflections on the Formation and the Distribution of Riches
creator: Turgot
description: Turgot's 1766 Réflexions — the physiocratic masterpiece: capital, interest, and the first marginal-utility reasoning — in the 1898 Macmillan English translation.

title: Œuvres économiques et philosophiques de F. Quesnay
creator: François Quesnay (Auguste Oncken, ed.)
description: Quesnay's complete economic and philosophical works — the Tableau économique and the physiocratic system — in Oncken's 1888 critical edition. French original; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: An Enquiry Concerning Political Justice, Vol. I
creator: William Godwin
description: Godwin's 1793 anarchist masterpiece — the first systematic statement of philosophical anarchism. Volume 1 of 2.

title: An Enquiry Concerning Political Justice, Vol. II
creator: William Godwin
description: Godwin's Political Justice, volume 2 — property, government, and the perfectibility of man. Volume 2 of 2, completing the work.

title: A Fragment on Government
creator: Jeremy Bentham (F. C. Montague, ed.)
description: Bentham's 1776 Fragment — the founding text of legal positivism and the first blast of utilitarian jurisprudence.

title: Theory of Legislation
creator: Jeremy Bentham (R. Hildreth, trans.)
description: Bentham's Theory of Legislation — the utilitarian science of law via Dumont's French redaction — in Hildreth's English translation.

title: Essays on Some Unsettled Questions of Political Economy
creator: John Stuart Mill
description: Mill's 1844 essays — the method of political economy, the definition of the science — written 1829-30, the methodological foundation of the Principles.

title: Les Confessions d'un révolutionnaire
creator: P.-J. Proudhon
description: Proudhon's 1851 Confessions — the revolutionary's autobiography and theory, from the February Revolution to the coup d'état. French original; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: The Conquest of Bread (1906 Putnam Edition)
creator: Peter Kropotkin
description: Kropotkin's 1906 anarchist-communist program — the conquest of bread, the classic statement of anarchist economics. 1906 G. P. Putnam's Sons edition; a 1926 Vanguard Press reprint is also held as kropotkin-conquest-bread-1906.

title: Fields, Factories and Workshops
creator: Peter Kropotkin
description: Kropotkin's 1913 Fields, Factories and Workshops — decentralization, the integration of industry and agriculture.

title: Memoirs of a Revolutionist, Vol. I
creator: Peter Kropotkin
description: Kropotkin's 1899 autobiography, volume 1 — from Russian prince to anarchist exile. Volume 1 of 2.

title: Memoirs of a Revolutionist, Vol. II
creator: Peter Kropotkin
description: Kropotkin's autobiography, volume 2 — completing the Memoirs. Volume 2 of 2.

title: Principles of Political Economy, Vol. I
creator: John Stuart Mill
description: Mill's 1848 Principles — the great Victorian synthesis of classical political economy. Volume 1 of 2.

title: Principles of Political Economy, Vol. II
creator: John Stuart Mill
description: Mill's Principles, volume 2 — completing the 1848 first edition. Volume 2 of 2.

title: Razvitie kapitalizma v Rossii (The Development of Capitalism in Russia)
creator: Vladimir Lenin
description: Lenin's 1899 'Development of Capitalism in Russia' — the Narodnik-Marxist debate, the empirical foundation of Russian Marxism. Russian original (as 'Vladimir Ilyin'); no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Massenstreik, Partei und Gewerkschaften
creator: Rosa Luxemburg
description: Luxemburg's 1906 Mass Strike pamphlet — the theory of the mass strike from the Russian Revolution of 1905. German original; no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Looking Backward: 2000-1887
creator: Edward Bellamy
description: Bellamy's 1888 utopian classic — Looking Backward from 2000 to 1887, the socialist Boston of the future.

title: News from Nowhere
creator: William Morris
description: Morris's 1890 utopian romance — News from Nowhere, the anarchist-socialist England of the future — in the 1892 Kelmscott Press edition.

title: L'Evangile selon le spiritisme
creator: Allan Kardec
description: The third book of Kardec's Spiritist canon: the moral maxims of Christ explained through Spiritism. Staged in the definitive 1866 Paris third edition (revue, corrigee et modifiee), in French — no 19th-century English translation exists (first English 1987, in copyright), so the PD French text is presented as a documentary edition.

title: Le Ciel et l'Enfer
creator: Allan Kardec
description: The fourth book of Kardec's Spiritist canon: divine justice, death, heaven, hell and purgatory examined through spirit communications. Staged in the 1865 Paris first edition, in French — the 1878 Blackwell/Trubner English translation survives only in libraries with no free scan, so the PD French text is presented as a documentary edition.

title: Genesis: The Miracles and the Predictions According to Spiritism
creator: Allan Kardec
description: The fifth and final book of Kardec's Spiritist canon: the Genesis narrative, miracles, and prophecies reconciled with science through Spiritism. First English translation (1883, Boston: Colby & Rich), 'translated by the spirit-guides of W. J. Colville.'

title: The Death-Blow to Spiritualism: Being the True Story of the Fox Sisters
creator: Reuben Briggs Davenport
description: Margaret Fox Kane's confession as told to New York World reporter Reuben Briggs Davenport — the insider account of the Fox sisters' rappings that broke the founding fraud story of modern spiritualism open. Work copyright 1888.

title: The Physical Phenomena of Spiritualism, Fraudulent and Genuine
creator: Hereward Carrington
description: Carrington's field manual of physical mediumship: the Palladino investigator's complete account of the most important historical phenomena, a criticism of their evidential value, and a full exposition of the methods used to reproduce them fraudulently. 1907 first edition.

title: The Present Age and Inner Life
creator: Andrew Jackson Davis
description: A sequel to Spiritual Intercourse: the Poughkeepsie Seer's harmonial-philosophy survey of the spiritualist movement's first five years — definitions of spiritualism, the spiritual congress, classifications of media and causes, and phenomena of the spiritual spheres. 1853 first edition.

title: Death and the After-Life
creator: Andrew Jackson Davis
description: Three discourses on death and the Summer Land: Davis's core statement of the spiritualist afterlife — the processes of death and the scenes of the after-life as perceived by the Poughkeepsie Seer. 1866 first edition.

description: Vol. vol2 of the SPR's journal of record (Parts V-VII): the central primary archive of the 1882-1930 evidential debate — telepathy experiments, apparition censuses, trance mediumship (Piper, Thompson), physical phenomena, and skeptical investigations.

creator: Society for Psychical Research
description: Vol. vol33 of the SPR's journal of record (Parts LXXXV-LXXXVIII): the central primary archive of the 1882-1930 evidential debate — telepathy experiments, apparition censuses, trance mediumship (Piper, Thompson), physical phenomena, and skeptical investigations.

title: Proceedings of the Society for Psychical Research, Vol. XXXVI (1926-1928)
creator: Society for Psychical Research
description: Vol. vol36 of the SPR's journal of record (Parts 97-103): the central primary archive of the 1882-1930 evidential debate — telepathy experiments, apparition censuses, trance mediumship (Piper, Thompson), physical phenomena, and skeptical investigations.

title: Neurypnology; or, The Rationale of Nervous Sleep, Considered in Relation with Animal Magnetism
creator: James Braid
description: The founding text of hypnotism: Braid coins 'neurypnology' and 'hypnotism' (1843), breaking mesmerism from animal-magnetism fluid theory into a neurophysiological account of trance. The single most-cited primary in hypnosis history; every history of the field starts here.

title: The Power of the Mind over the Body: An Experimental Inquiry into the Nature and Cause of the Phenomena Attributed by Baron Reichenbach and Others to a ‘New Imponderable’
creator: James Braid
description: Braid's experimental demolition of Reichenbach's 'odic force': the phenomena attributed to a new imponderable are shown to arise from the subject's own mind and body. The key document of Braid's anti-fluid, suggestion-centered turn.

title: Observations on Trance; or, Human Hybernation
creator: James Braid
description: Braid's monograph on trance states across cultures and history — fakirs, religious ecstatics, catalepsy — read as natural neurophysiological phenomena. The first comparative natural history of trance.

title: Hypnotic Therapeutics, Illustrated by Cases: With an Appendix on Table-Moving and Spirit-Rapping
creator: James Braid
description: Braid's clinical case-book of hypnotic cures, with his appendix debunking table-moving and spirit-rapping as unconscious muscular action — the earliest physiological account of the phenomena, predating the SPR by decades.

title: Magic, Witchcraft, Animal Magnetism, Hypnotism, and Electro-Biology
creator: James Braid
description: Braid's mature synthesis (3rd edition, greatly enlarged, 1852): witchcraft, demonic possession, and mesmeric marvels re-read as misapprehended nervous and psychological phenomena. The capstone of his demystification project.

title: The Philosophy of Electrical Psychology: In a Course of Twelve Lectures
creator: John Bovee Dods
description: The founding American statement of 'electrical psychology': Dods's twelve lectures arguing that mind acts on body through an electrical nervous medium. The pivotal text of the U.S. mesmeric movement and the seed of the New Thought mental-healing lineage.

title: Spirit Manifestations Examined and Explained
creator: John Bovee Dods
description: Dods's 1854 examination of the spirit-rappings craze, refuting Judge Edmonds's spirit hypothesis with an electrical-psychology account. A primary document of the mesmerism-to-spiritualism transition, from the mesmerist side.

title: Facts in Mesmerism, with Reasons for a Dispassionate Inquiry into It
creator: Chauncy Hare Townshend
description: The literary-philosophical case for mesmerism: Townshend's 1840 record of cases and argument that the phenomena deserve dispassionate scientific inquiry. The most-cited early English defense outside the medical journals.

title: Letters to a Candid Inquirer, on Animal Magnetism
creator: William Gregory
description: The standard British manual of animal magnetism: Gregory's letters systematizing the evidence for the magnetic sleep, clairvoyance, and mesmeric cure. The textbook form in which mid-Victorian Britain learned mesmerism.

title: Mesmerism and Its Opponents: A Narrative of Cases
creator: George Sandby
description: Sandby's 1844 narrative of cases answering the early British critics of mesmerism. A primary record of the first wave of English mesmeric controversy, with detailed case histories.

title: Somnolism and Psycheism, otherwise Vital Magnetism, or Mesmerism
creator: Joseph Haddock
description: Haddock's 1849 lectures (first edition) on somnolism and 'psycheism' — mesmeric clairvoyance treated physiologically and philosophically, with an appendix of mesmeric and 'psychical' experiments. A key provincial-English voice of the movement.

title: An Introduction to the Study of Animal Magnetism
creator: Baron Jules Dupotet de Sennevoy
description: The English translation (1838) of the French school leader's introduction: du Potet's systematization of magnetic practice, with the appendix of British practitioners' reports. The bridge text between the French and English mesmeric movements.

title: The Celestial Telegraph; or, Secrets of the Life to Come Revealed through Magnetism
creator: Louis Alphonse Cahagnet
description: Cahagnet's somnambulist visions of the afterlife (English 1850, from the 1848 French): eight 'ecstatics' describing the soul's post-mortem state under magnetism. The pivotal bridge text from mesmerism to spiritualism.

title: Traité du somnambulisme
creator: Alexandre Bertrand
description: Bertrand's 1823 French treatise on somnambulism and its modifications — the first systematic French pathology of magnetic sleep, foundational for the later French school (French original).

title: De la cause du sommeil lucide, ou Étude de la nature de l'homme
creator: Abbé Faria
description: Faria's 1819 work: the first statement of suggestion theory — lucid sleep produced not by magnetic fluid but by the subject's own concentration and the operator's command. The precursor text Braid himself cites (French original).

title: Annie Besant: An Autobiography
creator: Annie Besant
description: Besant's own life story through freethought, socialism, and her 1889 conversion to Theosophy: the indispensable primary for the Adyar succession and the movement's turn toward social and political engagement.

title: The Zoist: A Journal of Cerebral Physiology & Mesmerism, Vol. I (March 1843 to January 1844)
creator: John Elliotson (editor)
description: Vol. I of The Zoist (1843–1856), the first and most important English journal devoted to mesmerism and cerebral physiology, founded by John Elliotson. Thirteen volumes form the movement's complete primary record: surgical cases, somnambulist reports, and the mesmerism-to-hypnotism debate.

title: The Story of Atlantis: A Geographical, Historical and Ethnological Sketch
creator: W. Scott-Elliot
description: W. Scott-Elliot's The Story of Atlantis (first printed 1896) — the theosophical canon's Atlantis: root races, sub-races and cataclysms, with four maps. The companion to The Lost Lemuria; together they defined the Theosophical Society's lost-continent doctrine.

title: The Lost Lemuria
creator: W. Scott-Elliot
description: W. Scott-Elliot's The Lost Lemuria (first printed 1904) — the theosophical Lemuria: geological and biological evidence marshalled for the sunken southern continent, with two maps. The companion to The Story of Atlantis.

title: Abury, a Temple of the British Druids, with Some Others, Described
creator: William Stukeley
description: William Stukeley's Abury (1743) — the great Avebury survey: the serpent-temple, the Druidic plan, Phoenician origins. The companion to his Stonehenge (1740, already held); together they invented the Druidic megalith.

title: Thy Kingdom Come
creator: Charles Taze Russell
description: Charles Taze Russell's Thy Kingdom Come (1891) — the third volume of Millennial Dawn (Studies in the Scriptures), carrying the Great Pyramid chapters that made pyramidology a doctrine of the Bible Student movement. Document of record, not endorsement.

title: Great Pyramid Passages and Chambers, Vol. II
creator: John Edgar and Morton Edgar
description: John and Morton Edgar's Great Pyramid Passages and Chambers, vol. II (1913) — the second volume of the Russell-era measurement canon, completing the set whose vol. I (1910) is already held.

title: A New Theory of the Earth
creator: William Whiston
description: William Whiston's A New Theory of the Earth (1696) — comet-impact diluvialism from Newton's successor at Cambridge: the Deluge as a comet's watery mantle, the earth's history from creation to conflagration.

title: An Essay Toward a Natural History of the Earth
creator: John Woodward
description: John Woodward's An Essay Toward a Natural History of the Earth (1695) — diluvial stratigraphy: fossils as Flood relics, the earth's crust settled from the Deluge's waters. The great contemporary answer to Burnet.

title: The Sacred Theory of the Earth, Vol. I: The Deluge and Paradise
creator: Thomas Burnet
description: Thomas Burnet's The Sacred Theory of the Earth, vol. I (English 1684) — the two first books, concerning the Deluge and concerning Paradise: the founding modern catastrophist cosmology, in the English translation.

title: The Sacred Theory of the Earth, Vol. II: The Burning of the World and the New Heavens
creator: Thomas Burnet
description: Thomas Burnet's The Sacred Theory of the Earth, vol. II (English 1690) — the two last books, concerning the burning of the world and the new heavens and new earth, with the review of the theory and its proofs.

title: An Inquiry into the Original State and Formation of the Earth
creator: John Whitehurst
description: John Whitehurst's An Inquiry into the Original State and Formation of the Earth (1778) — strata, subterranean fire and the Deluge from the Derbyshire naturalist; the bridge between diluvialism and the coming geological revolution.

title: A Treatise on the Deluge
creator: Alexander Catcott
description: Alexander Catcott's A Treatise on the Deluge (1761) — the Hutchinsonian deluge: Moses's philosophy against Newton, the Flood as the earth's great agent. With remarks on the Bishop of Clogher's account.

title: The New Geology
creator: George McCready Price
description: George McCready Price's The New Geology (1923) — the founding textbook of flood geology: a young earth, the Flood as the geological agent, against the uniformitarian consensus. Document of record, not endorsement.

title: Chorea Gigantum; or, The Most Famous Antiquity of Great Britain, Vulgarly Called Stone-Heng
creator: Walter Charleton
description: Walter Charleton's Chorea Gigantum (1663) — the contemporary reply to Inigo Jones: Stonehenge as a Danish coronation place, not a Roman temple. The first great Stonehenge controversy, Jones vs. Charleton.

title: Choir Gaure, Vulgarly Called Stonehenge, on Salisbury Plain
creator: John Wood
description: John Wood's Choir Gaure (1747) — the Bath architect's Stonehenge: described, restored and explained as a Druidic lunar temple. The architect's answer to Stukeley.

title: Antiquities, Historical and Monumental, of the County of Cornwall
creator: William Borlase
description: William Borlase's Antiquities, Historical and Monumental, of the County of Cornwall (1754) — the great Cornish corpus: stone circles, cromlechs, inscribed stones, and the Druidic antiquities of the far west.

title: Antiquities, Historical and Monumental, of the County of Cornwall (Second Edition)
creator: William Borlase
description: The second edition (1769) of Borlase's Antiquities of Cornwall — revised and enlarged, with the Observations: the mature statement of the great Cornish corpus.

title: How I Found the Lost Atlantis, the Source of All Civilization
creator: Paul Schliemann
description: Paul Schliemann's 'How I Found the Lost Atlantis' (New York American, October 20, 1912) — the alleged grandson of Heinrich Schliemann's front-page Atlantis letters: the sealed envelope, the owl-headed vase, the orichalcum coins. The canonical Atlantis hoax document; presented as a document of the myth, not as fact.

title: The Great Pyramid: Its Divine Message
creator: David Davidson and Herbert Aldersmith
description: David Davidson and Herbert Aldersmith's The Great Pyramid: Its Divine Message (1924), vol. I: Pyramid Records — the metrological summa that reconciled Petrie's survey with Smyth's pyramidology: 568 pages coordinating historical documents and archaeological evidences.

title: Lectures on Homoeopathic Philosophy
creator: James Tyler Kent
description: James Tyler Kent's Lectures on Homoeopathic Philosophy (1900) — the philosophical foundation of American homeopathy: vital force, susceptibility, the single remedy, potentization. The system behind the Repertory.

title: Homoeopathy, the Science of Therapeutics
creator: Carroll Dunham
description: Carroll Dunham's Homoeopathy, the Science of Therapeutics (1877) — collected papers elucidating and illustrating the law of similars: the American school's great theoretical statement.

title: Text Book of Materia Medica
creator: Adolph Lippe
description: Adolph Lippe's Text Book of Materia Medica (1866) — the Hahnemannian purist's materia medica: characteristic symptoms, single remedy, high potencies. The doctrinal materia medica of strict Hahnemannianism.

title: Leaders in Homoeopathic Therapeutics
creator: E. B. Nash
description: E. B. Nash's Leaders in Homoeopathic Therapeutics (1899) — the beloved clinical digest: leading remedies in homoeopathic therapeutics, arranged for the prescriber. The most-used homeopathic handbook of its era.

title: The American Eclectic Dispensatory
creator: John King
description: John King's American Eclectic Dispensatory (1854) — the eclectic materia medica: botanical remedies, their preparation and uses, from the Cincinnati school. The dispensatory of American botanical medicine.

title: Specific Medication and Specific Medicines
creator: John Milton Scudder
description: John Milton Scudder's Specific Medication and Specific Medicines (1870) — the eclectic systematizer's doctrine: specific indications for specific remedies, studied by the drug's direct action. The method-book of later eclecticism.

title: Philosophy of Osteopathy
creator: Andrew Taylor Still
description: Andrew Taylor Still's Philosophy of Osteopathy (1899) — the founder's statement: the body as machine, structure governing function, the lesion as the cause of disease. The founding text of osteopathy.

title: Autobiography of Andrew T. Still
creator: Andrew Taylor Still
description: Andrew Taylor Still's Autobiography (1897) — with a history of the discovery and development of the science of osteopathy: the founder's life, the Civil War surgeon's path to a new healing science.

title: My Water Cure
creator: Sebastian Kneipp
description: Sebastian Kneipp's My Water Cure (English 1892) — hydrotherapy tested through thirty years: affusions, baths, herbs and regimen from the Bavarian priest who made the water cure a world movement.

title: Practical Instruction in Animal Magnetism
creator: J. P. F. Deleuze
description: J. P. F. Deleuze's Practical Instruction in Animal Magnetism (English 1843) — the French mesmeric manual: the method, the crises, the ethics of magnetic practice, from the librarian of the Paris Museum.

title: The Lesser Writings of Samuel Hahnemann
creator: Samuel Hahnemann
description: The Lesser Writings of Samuel Hahnemann (1852) — collected minor works, essays and case notes, edited by R. E. Dudgeon with annotations by Richard Hughes: the founder's occasional writings outside the Organon and materia medicas.

title: Organon of Medicine (Sixth Edition)
creator: Samuel Hahnemann
description: Hahnemann's Organon of Medicine, sixth edition (completed 1842; English 1922, trans. William Boericke) — the final text of homeopathy's founding work: the LM potencies, the mature doctrine, published eighty years after the manuscript was finished.

title: A Manual of Pharmacodynamics
creator: Richard Hughes
description: Richard Hughes's A Manual of Pharmacodynamics (1867) — British homeopathy's systematizer: the actions of drugs arranged for therapeutic study, the bridge between materia medica and practice.

title: Universal Naturopathic Encyclopedia
creator: Benedict Lust
description: Benedict Lust's Universal Naturopathic Encyclopedia, Directory and Buyers' Guide (1918) — the year-book of drugless therapy: the organizer of American naturopathy gathers the whole drugless field.

title: Toxemia Explained: The True Interpretation of the Cause of Disease
creator: John Henry Tilden
description: John Henry Tilden's Toxemia Explained (1926) — the toxemia doctrine: all disease as the body's response to retained metabolic waste, cured by rest, fasting and right living. The natural-hygiene classic.

title: The Guiding Symptoms of Our Materia Medica, Vol. I
creator: Constantine Hering
description: Constantine Hering's The Guiding Symptoms of Our Materia Medica, vol. I (1879) — the great American materia medica: guiding symptoms arranged by bodily region, the clinical distillation of a lifetime's provings.
